fullText:
Update: A day later, GPT-6 Astra is rolling out to Business and Pro customers on the $100/month or $200/month plan. This follows other new model releases before Plus customers on the $20/month plan gain access.

Update #2: A few hours later, Plus users with the $20/month subscription now have Astra access as well. 

It’s been just over a year since OpenAI released the first GPT-5 models for ChatGPT. Now it’s time for GPT-6 Astra to upgrade ChatGPT and Codex capabilities. Details below.

GPT-6 Astra details

OpenAI has officially detailed its new model, GPT-6 Astra, which it calls “the world’s most intelligent and aligned model.”

Here’s more from the official announcement today:

GPT‑6 Astra brings together years of research and big bets across pre-training, reinforcement learning, and alignment. Astra is state-of-the-art on computer use, browsing, software engineering, cybersecurity, science, and professional work. Astra saturates FrontierMath Tier 4 with a 98% score, having already helped solve long-standing open problems⁠ in mathematics. Astra also saturates ARC-AGI-3 with a 99.9% score and ExploitBench with a 100% score. It also sets a new frontier on computer and browser use, handling the most demanding professional work with unmatched speed, accuracy, and judgment. 

OpenAI goes further on how GPT-6 improves computer use, which allows ChatGPT to use your Mac or other desktop, including in the background while you work:

GPT‑6 Astra pairs advances in computer use with targeted training for professional environments, to help tackle complex work tasks. It combines the intelligence required for complex problems with the ability to carry out multistep workflows and produce polished documents, spreadsheets, and presentations.

Additionally, GPT-6 Astra is “the best model for software engineering to date,” OpenAI says.

With Astra, ChatGPT is nearly 2x faster at computer use than before.

In addition to the amazing new model, we’ve optimized the harness to make computer use run much faster.

These optimizations work in existing models too, so tasks are sped up by ~60% in GPT-5.6 Sol. Try it! pic.twitter.com/2EXH5f0uZL

— Ari Weinstein (@AriX) September 4, 2026

In terms of Codex specifically, here’s something new about GPT-6:

With Astra, we’re introducing a new way for Codex to preserve and retrieve context when the context window fills. Historically, models have used compaction to summarize work during long sessions, such as when debugging complex issues or tackling large refactors. Each compaction can leave out details about why a fix failed or how a component behaves. In Codex, Astra can keep notes across context windows, preserving accumulated details without repeatedly compressing them into a single summary. Earlier context windows remain searchable, so Astra can find requirements or test results from previous messages and tool outputs—even if that information wasn’t captured in its notes. You can enable this experimental feature in your Codex, and it will become the default for Astra in the coming weeks.

we launched a thing…

it is best in class at computer use, scientific research, coding, math, professional work like making slides, and so much more.

it is superhuman at ingesting enormous amounts of context. so patient. so relentless. so good at context switching. and it will… https://t.co/l3yM1Sy68n

— Kundan Kumar (@kundan2510) September 3, 2026

OpenAI calls GPT-6 Astra a “significant jump in cyber capabilities,” adding that it “meets the Critical threshold⁠ in cybersecurity under our Preparedness Framework.”

For that reason, the model is rolling out slowly to users.

“GPT‑6 Astra is rolling out today to a limited set of organizations and over the coming days will become available to all ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise users, as well as through the OpenAI API and AWS,” OpenAI says. 

“Astra usage is included within the existing subscription allowances—users and businesses will also be able to purchase credits for additional usage. Users on the Pro, Business, and Enterprise plans will also get access to GPT‑6 Astra Pro. Enterprise administrators can enable Astra for their workspace; access is off by default at launch.”

The road to GPT-6 Astra

GPT-5 launched August 7, 2025, replacing GPT-4o and several reasoning models as ChatGPT’s default. Its defining feature was automatic routing: ChatGPT could answer quickly or invoke deeper reasoning depending on the request. OpenAI also claimed fewer factual errors than GPT-4o.

Apple adopted the model with iOS 26, iPadOS 26, and macOS Tahoe 26. ChatGPT requests passed through Apple Intelligence, including Siri handoffs, Writing Tools, and visual intelligence, switched from GPT-4o to GPT-5.

GPT-5.1 promised warmer, more natural answers in November. December’s “code red” GPT-5.2 accelerated professional work in response to Gemini. GPT-5.3 Instant targeted ChatGPT’s “cringe” tone, followed two days later by GPT-5.4 Thinking with a million-token context window and built-in computer use.

OpenAI subsequently added GPT-5.4 mini and nano, the restricted GPT-5.4-Cyber, GPT-5.5 for more autonomous work, GPT-5.5 Instant, and July’s GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra, and Luna models.

From the Codex Mac app to a new ChatGPT

The software around those models transformed too. OpenAI launched a dedicated Codex Mac app in February as a hub for running multiple coding agents, reviewing changes, and scheduling work.

In July, Codex effectively became the new ChatGPT desktop app, combining Chat, Work, and Codex while the previous native client was renamed ChatGPT Classic.

For me, Codex has changed how I work with ChatGPT the most. I’m able to offload a lot more work that doesn’t require critical thinking and even build tools on my Mac that I couldn’t put together otherwise.

GPT-6 availability

OpenAI says its new GPT-6 models will only be available to its cyber security-focused Daybreak program members to start. This echoes a similar release cadence with the previous model release, GPT-5.6. 

Here’s what OpenAI says about availability, specifically:

GPT‑6 Astra is rolling out today to a limited set of organizations and over the coming days will become available to all ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise users, as well as through the OpenAI API and AWS.

You can learn much more about OpenAI’s latest frontier model here.

title: Lenovo’s first RTX Spark laptops can have up to 128GB of RAM
snippet: IFA 2026 is underway with Lenovo’s Innovation World event seeing the debut of the company’s first RTX Spark laptops as well as a flagship Android tablet and more. more…
fullText:
IFA 2026 is underway with Lenovo’s Innovation World event seeing the debut of the company’s first RTX Spark laptops as well as a flagship Android tablet and more.

Starting off with laptops, Lenovo is using Nvidia’s new RTX Spark chip in new Yoga machines – and they sound nuts.

The Lenovo Yoga Pro 9n is a 15-inch with a 2560×1600 OLED display, up to 128GB of RAM, two SSD slots and up to 4TB of storage, and a 92.5Whr battery with 140W charging and a “Rapid Charge Express” mode that buys 3 hours of battery life in 15 minutes. For ports, it has two USB-C (40GBps) and two USB-A ports on either side, as well as HDMI and a full-size SD card slot. That’s all in a machine that’s “as thin as” 16.7mm and weighs 3.64lbs. It also has a haptic trackpad which has pen support.

Again, it sounds nuts.

	

The other option is the Yoga 9n 2-in-1 with a 16-inch display. It has a 2880×1800 OLED display, the same Nvidia RTX Spark chip, but is a bit tamer throughout the rest of the package. Up to 64GB of RAM, up to 2TB of SSD storage, but the same ports. Battery life is powered by a 99.9Whr battery with the same fast-charging setup, but this one is thicker at 17.5mm and weighs in at 4.28lbs.

Lenovo is directly positioning these machines at professional creators, with a focus on raw power for video editing, 3D rendering, and local AI applications. 

As you might imagine in the midst of RAMageddon, Lenovo isn’t confirming prices for either of these machines just yet, and there’s no release window either.

title: A hacker stole $340M in a crypto heist, then returned most of it
snippet: The latest heist is one of the largest thefts of cryptocurrency to date.
fullText:
In Brief

Posted:

7:11 AM PDT · September 8, 2026

Image Credits:Samuil Levich / Getty Images

		

							

											
									

					

	

A hacker stole thousands of bitcoins worth about $340 million in a heist at a settlement exchange used by several cryptocurrency exchanges, representing one of the largest known thefts of crypto this year.

Liquid Network, launched in 2018 by crypto firm Blockstream, said in a post on X on Sunday that a “white hat” hacker stole the funds from the network’s wallet, and that it has paused operations until the incident is resolved.

It’s not yet known who the hacker is, but crypto media reports that the hacker allegedly exploited a bug to withdraw the funds. The hacker said they would return the funds if Blockstream fixed the bug.

Former Blockstream executive Samson Mow said in a post on X on Monday that the company had fixed the bug, and around 3,400 of the roughly 4,000 stolen bitcoins had been returned. The remaining about 600 bitcoins (about $47 million) were still under the hacker’s control.

Mow said operations will remain paused until additional fixes and security improvements are made prior to restarting.

The theft ranks as one of the largest heists of digital funds to date, according to the Rekt leaderboard, which tracks cryptocurrency thefts.

title: Apple Vision Pro was just used in a first-of-its-kind surgery
snippet: We’ve seen several stories about Apple Vision Pro being used in healthcare settings. This week, Stryker announced the completion of the first surgical procedure using an innovative new app on Vision Pro. more…
fullText:
We’ve seen several stories about Apple Vision Pro being used in healthcare settings. This week, Stryker announced the completion of the first surgical procedure using an innovative new app on Vision Pro.

The surgery, a hip arthroscopy, was completed using SportSuite Vision, an app that brings “critical digital content into a surgeon’s virtual space.” This includes things like arthroscopic video, HipCheck, HipMap, and CT imaging.

Here’s how Stryker describes the app:

SportSuite Vision brings critical digital content into a surgeon’s visual space, allowing them to see physical objects in the OR alongside digital tools such as arthroscopic images, HipCheck, HipMap and CT imaging.

During arthroscopic procedures, surgeons often rely on multiple displays positioned throughout the OR to access visualization and procedural data. By bringing multiple data sources into the surgeon’s field of view, the technology can reduce reliance on traditional monitors and support a more streamlined, ergonomic surgical workflow.

SportSuite Vision received FDA De Novo authorization on July 17. Stryker says this makes it the first app the FDA has authorized for intraoperative use with Vision Pro.

The hip arthroscopy was completed at Duke Health. Chad Mather III, the orthopedic surgeon who performed the operation, praised Vision Pro and SportSuite Vision:

“Using spatial computing enabled me to customize the placement of key clinical information to fit my workflow and access it within the sterile field. This helped create a more comfortable, streamlined OR setup while keeping the information I needed in view.”

You can learn more about SportSuite Vision on the Stryker website.

Also this week, Pfizer announced it is using Apple Vision Pro “to create an unforgettable, immersive experience” to “illustrate” its commitment to “outdo cancer.”

Pfizer’s bold mission is clear: Outdo cancer through relentless innovation and hope. To vividly illustrate this commitment for patients, healthcare providers, and internal stakeholders, Pfizer collaborated with Groove Jones to craft an immersive mixed reality experience that inspires as much as it informs. Apple Vision Pro’s ability to seamlessly blend digital and real worlds provided the perfect canvas to emotionally connect audiences and showcase Pfizer’s oncology leadership.

You can get a closer look at the experience on the Groove Jones website.

title: Three new iPhones launch this week, here’s what’s coming
snippet: Apple’s big September event is this Wednesday, and the company has three new iPhone models set to launch: iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and iPhone Ultra. Here’s what to expect. more…
fullText:
Apple’s big September event is this Wednesday, and the company has three new iPhone models set to launch: iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and iPhone Ultra. Here’s what to expect.

iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max

iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max are coming as successors to Apple’s popular 17 Pro line.

New features that are rumored include:

A20 Pro chip for more power and efficiency

Major camera upgrades, especially to the Main camera with variable aperture

35% smaller Dynamic Island for more modern design

New colors, headlined by a bold burgundy

Best battery life ever, with iPhone 18 Pro Max getting big gains

Camera Control gets a revamp

C2 cellular modem designed by Apple

New satellite features, including 5G

iPhone 18 Pro is also expected to have a higher starting price. Estimates suggest it could start at $1,399, but I suspect it could be closer to $1,199 or $1,249.

iPhone Ultra

iPhone Ultra is the rumored name for Apple’s first foldable, with its expected $2,000+ price creating a new high-end tier.

The foldable form factor should make iPhone Ultra the most radically unique model Apple has yet introduced. It will have a wide book-style fold, with a roughly 5.4-inch outer display and 7.8-inch inner display that resembles an iPad mini.

Design materials are expected to mimic the iPhone Air, with a titanium border and sleek look.

iPhone Ultra will have two rear cameras (Main and Ultra Wide) plus two front-facing cameras, one for each display. It will use Touch ID for authentication rather than Face ID.

Software will be where the device especially shines, with iOS 27 supporting side-by-side app multitasking and adaptive landscape layouts that are perfect for the new form factor.

Performance should be about the same as iPhone 18 Pro, with the same A20 Pro chip, a vapor chamber for cooling, and a C2 modem.

What’s missing: iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2

Normally we would expect a new base model iPhone 18 to launch in September too, alongside an iPhone Air successor.

This year though, Apple is reportedly overhauling its fall lineup by pushing the iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2 into early 2027.

It’s unknown whether this change is entirely strategic, or simply out of necessity due to the current memory crisis. In any case, the absence of more affordable models means this fall’s new iPhone line will focus solely on the high end.

title: Google Maps speedometer disappears on Android Auto for some, traffic data still missing too
snippet: Android Auto users are reporting an issue where the Google Maps speedometer, available for mere months, is randomly vanishing. more…
fullText:
Android Auto users are reporting an issue where the Google Maps speedometer, available for mere months, is randomly vanishing.

Back in July, Google Maps on Android Auto finally started rolling out support for a live speedometer while navigating. This was alongside showing speed limits. It started more broadly rolling out later that month, but still hasn’t rolled out to everyone.

Now, in fact, we’re looking at the exact opposite happening. A number of users have reported on Reddit that the speedometer has suddenly vanished on Android Auto. It’s not a particularly widespread issue, it seems, but the rollout hasn’t expanded to all users in the first place. This is alongside traffic patterns, which are still missing for a number of users after breaking in late August. 

We’ve also noticed continued reports of Android Auto missing its signal indicator, an ongoing bug for months at this point.

	

Google rolls out new Android Auto updates on a pretty regular basis, along with Maps, but these isolated issues just don’t seem to be going away. Leave a comment below if you’re running into these problems.

title: OpenAI releases ChatGPT Images 2.5 with ‘sharper details’ and ‘more precise editing’
snippet: In April, OpenAI released upgraded image generation technology with ChatGPT Images 2. Five months later, the company is releasing an enhanced version, ChatGPT Images 2.5. more…
fullText:
In April, OpenAI released upgraded image generation technology with ChatGPT Images 2. Five months later, the company is releasing an enhanced version, ChatGPT Images 2.5. 

ChatGPT Images 2 was a notable leap over the company’s earlier image generation tools.

It added 2K resolution output, multiple aspect ratio support, and the ability to use web research for up-to-date information. Images 2 also added non-Latin language expertise and two intelligence levels: Instant and Thinking.

The latest Images 2.5 version touts “sharper details, faster generation, more precise editing, and better tools for creating and sharing.”

“Images 2.5 produces more natural lighting and richer textures, is better at preserving the subjects in your reference photos, and follows editing instructions more reliably across multiple turns,” OpenAI says.

“We’ve also reduced image generation latency by up to 50% compared with Images 2.0, so you can generate images and refine your concepts more quickly.”

Additionally, the company details a new “Sketch” feature that enables drawing directly in ChatGPT. This can be used as a reference for image generation. Plus OpenAI is introducing templates for popular image formats, prompt sharing for others to try your ideas related to image-gen, and more.

Additionally, OpenAI is releasing two versions of Images 2.5 for developers to build around in their apps. GPT-Image-2.5 Flare and GPT-Image-2.5 Sunburt will be available through OpenAI’s API:

GPT‑Image‑2.5 Flare brings the same improvements in quality, editing, and speed to the API and is the default choice for most applications, delivering higher-quality images than GPT‑Image‑2 at 50% lower latency. It’s well suited to everything from creator and social content to product experiences, visual search, rapid image prototyping, and high-volume generation.

GPT‑Image‑2.5 Sunburst is built for premium visual workflows that benefit from tighter control across edits. Use it for creative and editing workflows like production-ready campaign creative or polished product imagery.

“Images 2.5 is rolling out today to ChatGPT, ChatGPT Work, and Codex users across all tiers on desktop, mobile, and web,” according to OpenAI. You can learn more about the new image-gen technology here.

Today’s ChatGPT Images 2.5 release follows last week’s GPT-6 Astra launch.

title: Gemini 3.8 Flash rolling out three weeks after last release
snippet: After the last model release three weeks ago, Google today is rolling out Gemini 3.8 Flash. This marks the third Flash update in three months. more…
fullText:
After the last model release three weeks ago, Google today is rolling out Gemini 3.8 Flash. This marks the third Flash update in three months.

…our most intelligent workhorse model, delivering significant improvements from 3.7 Flash across software engineering, agentic tasks, and critical, multi-step reasoning in specialized domains.

Gemini 3.8 Flash “delivers substantial gains” over its predecessor in various benchmarks, with Google also noting how it is “often approaching the performance of higher-cost frontier models.”

On DeepSWE v1.1 (Long-Horizon Software Engineering) 3.8 Flash outperforms most larger frontier models in autonomously solving complex engineering problems end to end, only at a fraction of the cost.

In quantitative and professional fields that require advanced analysis and reporting, 3.8 Flash outperforms 3.7 Flash and other frontier models in benchmarks like Vals Finance Agent V2 and Harvey’s Legal Agent Benchmark. 

3.8 Flash also achieves a 54.9% on HLE-Verified, demonstrating its ability to handle multi-step reasoning across STEM, humanities, and professional fields.

Google says these “performance gains stem from a core design choice: 3.8 Flash works harder.”

On complex tasks, it exhibits greater diligence — executing extra reasoning steps, and calling tools iteratively. At times, the model might use more tokens to maximize performance, especially at higher effort levels.

Note: Updated DeepSWE v1.1 score

	

Similar to the previous model, Gemini 3.8 Flash’s knowledge cutoff date is March 2026 “for some domains while in others [users] may experience the model’s knowledge is limited to January 2025.”

Google is once again offering an introductory price of $0.75/1M input tokens and $3.75/1M output tokens until December 31.

Gemini 3.8 Flash is already live in the Gemini app for Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers, AI Mode, and Gemini in Google Sheets. It’s also available for developers in Google Antigravity, AI Studio, and the Gemini API.

Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber

Google today also announced Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber (replacing 3.5) for trusted testers — via a new Fairwind Program — with “frontier-level performance in autonomous vulnerability discovery.”

The Chrome Security team found that 3.8 Flash Cyber produced 2.6 times more correct patches to vulnerabilities in Chrome than the best commercial models that are much larger.

Wiz found that Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber achieves +7.5-9.7% higher recall on their internal penetration testing benchmark for a 2.3-5.2x lower cost compared to other leading frontier models.

Google’s Cloud Vulnerability Research team leveraged the 3.8 Flash Cyber model to find a critical foundational vulnerability in less than 2 hours, a vulnerability for which research and discovery usually takes months.

title: Google stops selling ‘Certified Refurbished’ Pixel 7 series, still no Pixel 9 yet
snippet: Google has pulled refurbished Pixel 7 devices from its store, with the Pixel 9 yet to make its debut. more…
fullText:
Google has pulled refurbished Pixel 7 devices from its store, with the Pixel 9 yet to make its debut.

On the Google Store you can buy a “Certified Refurbished” Pixel smartphone at a lower price, usually hundreds off of the original retail price. While it’s not always the best deal compared to a used device on the private market, there’s considerable peace of mind in buying a refurbished device directly from Google seeing as every device comes with a one-year warranty, gets a full inspection with replacement parts, and is sold unlocked for use with any carrier. These devices are also available on Amazon.

But the options have now shrunk.

Google now only has the Pixel 8 series – 8, Pro, and 8a – available alongside the Pixel 7a, with prices ranging from $289 to $649. The Pixel 7 series has been removed in the past few days, with its final appearance on the Wayback Machine in late August. Google was running a promotion where refurbished Pixel 7 devices included a free Pixel Watch 2 from July up until the past week or so.

	

This doesn’t come as a huge surprise. The Pixel 7 series launched in 2022 and will stop getting updates in the latter half of 2027. What’s more of a surprise is that the Pixel 9 series has yet to arrive in Google’s refurbished program. With Pixel 11 now available, it’s likely the Pixel 9 will arrive in the coming weeks. Pixel 8 was added in October 2025, roughly two months after the Pixel 10’s debut.

title: Google Pixel adding ‘Battery usage summaries,’ rolling out on Pixel 10 and newer
snippet: Google is rolling out a new AI-generated feature on Pixel 10 and Pixel 11 devices called “Battery usage summaries” which translate battery use stats into natural language. more…
fullText:
Google is rolling out a new AI-generated feature on Pixel 10 and Pixel 11 devices called “Battery usage summaries” which translate battery use stats into natural language.

Rolling out via an AI Core update on Pixel 10 and Pixel 11 devices, “Battery usage summaries” deliver on a rather simple premise. On your battery usage page, a new AI-generated overview summarizes your battery usage, pulling in recent history and calling out more powerful apps. 

On a support page, Google explains:

At the top of the Battery usage page, you can get a personalized summary of your battery usage. It summarizes these analyses, which are performed in the background:

Identifies apps that consume the most battery.

Monitors app background activity.

Compares the overall and app-specific battery consumption between your selected period and recent average.

The feature is enabled by default on supported Pixels, but can be turned off via Settings > Battery & charging > Battery Usage > Battery usage summaries (overflow menu). A screenshot sent to Android Authority shows an example of what the summary might say beyond the “you’ve barely used your phone” vibes our unused-for-the-day Pixel 11 Pro Fold shows. Google says that “outputs vary and highlight the most important info only.”

	

Google’s support page mentions that the latest AI Core update is needed to enable the feature, but it’s unclear if there are any additional requirements. While we’re seeing the feature live on both a Pixel 11 Pro Fold and a Pixel 11 Pro XL, it’s not yet showing on Pixel 10 or Pixel 10a devices we’ve updated and tested.

If you’re seeing “Battery usage summaries” on your Pixel, let us know in the comments below.

title: Anker is combining its Eufy, Soundcore, and brands into two ‘Anker’ groups
snippet: At IFA 2026, Anker is not only unveiling a bunch of new products, but also announcing that it is merging all of its core brands into one – sort of – with Eufy, Soundcore, and others going away. more…
fullText:
At IFA 2026, Anker is not only unveiling a bunch of new products, but also announcing that it is merging all of its core brands into one – sort of – with Eufy, Soundcore, and others going away.

Existing Anker products are sold under the Anker, Soundcore, Eufy, EufyMake, and Solix brands. It can be a bit confusing, especially when these brands overlap here and there. But, now, everything is merging under a single “Anker” name, but with two groups. “Anker for You” will handle things like charging, audio, personal health, and “creative tools,” while “Anker for Home” will cover security, robotics, and home energy. 

Anker says this change will happen gradually as new products are released, with existing products also moving over to the new branding in time. This also comes as the first Anker retail store is opening this weekend in Berlin. Notably, some products will have both “Anker” and other older brand names together.

At IFA, Anker has a host of new products being announced. “Anker for You” launches include:

	

Anker Soundcore AeroClip 2 Pro & AeroClip 2 open-ear earbuds

Space 2 Pro over-ear headphones with up to 60-hour battery life

Liberty Buds 2 

Sleep 4 & Sleep 4 Pro sleep earbuds with PPG, heart rate, and HRV tracking

SleepLab & SleepLab Pro sleep speaker with nightlight, radar-based sleep tracking

MagGo Power Bank 2 Pro Qi2 25W battery bank with active cooling, 10,000 mAh

Anker Laptop Charger Pro which recognizes your laptop model for best battery health

Anker MagStand Charging Station with Qi2 25W pad, retractable USB-C cable, and another USB-C port. 

“Anker for Home” launches include:

Anker MindBase local AI hub for smart home devices

Anker Eufy TrackLight Cam S1 with auto-tracking light and 4K telephoto camera

Video Doorbell S4 with 180-degree panoramic view

Anker Eufy Robot Vacuum Omni E35 with lower noise, self-cleaning roller mop, 35,000 Pa suction

title: Why Miele Put a Camera Inside Its Latest Dishwasher
snippet: Miele’s latest dishwasher has smarts a-plenty, including a camera housed in the back of the door.
fullText:
It seems the public wants fewer cameras, not more, but that hasn’t stopped the large appliance industry. While a fridge or oven camera almost certainly presents less of a privacy risk than a Flock surveillance unit — hey, it’s right there in the name — one could argue they’ve gone overboard. 

Sensors and lenses have crept into nearly every other kitchen machine, met with a range of consumer sentiment. Smart ovens and connected refrigerators aren’t new, but a camera-equipped dishwasher?  When I heard that Miele snuck one inside its latest model, the Diamond G8 unveiled at IFA 2026 in Berlin, I was suspicious. After a rep walked me through the new machine’s novel smart features, the reasoning came somewhat into focus.

A camera in Miele’s new dishwasher helps it choose the best cycle.

An AI-powered camera recognizes dish types to help pick a cycle

The small camera, fixed to the back of the dishwasher door, gets a clear shot of the dishwasher’s interior. It uses that view to take inventory of what’s inside, recognizing dozens of common kitchen items and tailoring the wash cycle and detergent volume accordingly.

The Diamond G8 is one of the smartest dishwashers we’ve encountered, and it’s easy on the eyes.

Got portable bottles or reusable straws in the dedicated slots? The dishwasher’s brain recognizes them and makes sure those items get the spritz they need. Load it up with pots and pans, and the camera identifies them, triggering a more intensive cycle so everything comes out clean. A smaller load prompts a lighter cycle, so you’re not wasting hot water or soap.

The G8 recognizes straws, flatware, silverware and cookware and adjusts its cycle for optimized cleaning.

The camera also determines how full the dishwasher is. Command the G8 to start when it reaches, say, 80% capacity, and it’ll monitor the load and automatically begin a cycle once it hits that threshold. 

One of my favorite features has nothing to do with the camera

The G8 Diamond takes advantage of fluctuations in electricity prices throughout the day. Tell it to run when electricity is cheapest, and the dishwasher waits for those lower-cost hours before starting its cycle. It’s a small detail, but it points to where Miele – and kitchen appliances more broadly – seem to be headed: machines that don’t just perform a task, but figure out the best and most efficient way to do it.

The dishwasher can be programmed to run when energy costs are cheapest in your area.

Miele’s newly unveiled machine has other AI-powered features that encourage efficiency and performance.  The G8 features careful water and energy monitoring, which you can track through Miele’s app. It also includes a smart detergent-dispensing system, first introduced by the brand in 2018, and a beefed-up hot-air drying system that Miele says gets dishes bone-dry every time.

The camera paired with a smart detergent dispenser doles out just the right amount of soap. 

Miele plans to roll out the Diamond G8 in the European market later this year as it considers a North American strategy, according to a spokesperson. 

A retail price is still under wraps, but I expect it to land in the super-premium zone. For a top-performing dishwasher you can buy today, see our list of the best models in 2026.

title: Besxar is building an orbital semiconductor factory, one SpaceX rocket at a time
snippet: If you want to manufacture in space—and bring the products back again—there’s a limited set of options: Wait to go to the International Space Station, or partner with a handful of start-ups launching spacecraft that spend time in orbit before they return to Earth. But the vehicle that goes to space and comes back to […]
fullText:
If you want to manufacture in space—and bring the products back again—there’s a limited set of options: Wait to go to the International Space Station, or partner with a handful of start-ups launching spacecraft that spend time in orbit before they return to Earth.

But the vehicle that goes to space and comes back to Earth more often than any other is a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket booster, which made that round-trip 163 times last year and has already flown more than 100 times this year. Now, a startup says it has talked Elon Musk’s space company into letting it prototype an orbital semiconductor factory across a dozen flights with the booster.

Besxar, a start-up founded by former OpenAI staffer Ashley Pilipiszyn, wants to make the key precursors for advanced semiconductors by taking advantage of the vacuum of space. A key reason chip fabs on Earth are such hugely insane infrastructure projects is the need to create pressurized clean rooms to keep out even microscopic dust and contaminants that could ruin a chip during production. Pilipiszyn argues that a new generation of rockets could offer an alternative to all that infrastructure and to do it, she has raised almost $14 million, including a $9 million seed round led by Dauntless Ventures and Overture VC.

“We’re at a time where it’s actually more cost-effective to go where the physics already works,” she told TechCrunch.  “Don’t do it on Earth where you’re fighting physics.”

The company’s first two “fabships”—small canisters designed to carry and test semiconductor materials in orbit—flew on a July Starlink mission and were intended to prove that the canisters could survive a launch, protect wafer samples from contamination, and expose them to the vacuum of space. Besxar succeeded in these objectives despite a malfunction in the flight data system in one canister, which the company is currently investigating.

“The flown samples were the cleanest and had the least amount of particulate matter compared to … non-flown terrestrial wafers, which is fantastic for us as we scale up,” Pilipiszyn told TechCrunch.

Besxar expects to keep iterating over the next two years, with the ultimate goal of flying larger fabs onboard a vehicle like SpaceX’s Starship, the company’s next-generation rocket still in development. Pilipiszyn first approached SpaceX three years ago to talk about buying flights on Starship and eventually settled on the booster payload deal as a way to de-risk her technology in the meantime. Next up is heating the wafers, then depositing one material on the wafers, then two materials, and so forth.

Once it is producing qualification samples, Besxar—named after “beskar,” the metal used in Star Wars to make Mandalorian armor—wants to supply leading chipmakers with the wafers used to make the kinds of advanced chips that regulate electrical power in data centers, robots and electric vehicles.

There are a number of companies working to leverage the space environment for higher-quality semiconductors, including United Semiconductors and Space Forge, but all face the same difficulty: the limited ability to return a meaningful volume of product. Pilipiszyn expects to start to scale up to hundreds and then thousands of wafers per fab, but that path depends on cheap rockets. That in turn requires SpaceX to get Starship operational—or competitors like Rocket Lab and Stoke Space getting their own next-generation rockets off the ground.

“We believe that there is a solid transport layer now, so we can focus on the application layer,” she told TechCrunch. “We can just focus on our core manufacturing and getting our products back down to earth to market as quickly as possible.”

He has closely covered the rise of the private space industry and is the author of  Rocket Billionaires: Elon Musk, Jeff Bezos and the New Space Race. title: Apple might soon make App Store changes to raise revenue, increase margins: report
snippet: According to the latest edition of the Power On newsletter from Mark Gurman, Apple is reportedly considering making some changes to its App Store. The goal? To increase the potential revenue it brings in. more…
fullText:
According to the latest edition of the Power On newsletter from Mark Gurman, Apple is reportedly considering making some changes to its App Store. The goal? To increase the potential revenue it brings in.

It isn’t exactly clear what changes Apple could have planned for the App Store. Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reports that Apple wants to “figure out ways to raise margins and squeeze additional recurring revenue from the platform,” and that this effort is largely driven by new CEO John Ternus and existing services SVP Eddy Cue.

Supposedly, this effort was part of the reason why longtime Apple executive Phil Schiller left the company last week. After departing from his role as marketing SVP in 2020, Schiller became an Apple Fellow – where part of his role was running the App Store. Schiller wasn’t a fan of the idea:

Schiller, on the other hand, seems to believe that such moves will only further irk developers and governments. While there was no internal blowup or anything like that, it’s something he wanted no part of.

There’s a multitude of ways Apple could potentially raise margins from the App Store. It could get rid of its manual app review process, which is likely costly and not super effective in the age of agentic coding. People likely wouldn’t appreciate further automation of app review, though it would certainly be a way to cut on costs.

	

It could charge more for its developer membership, currently priced at $99/year. Given the fact that many small developers are spending $200/mo for Codex and Claude subscriptions to develop apps, you could argue Apple could charge more and get away with it. The company could also charge large developers a subscription fee based on traffic, to offload some of the infrastructure costs.

Only time can tell what this will turn into, though I’m certainly interested to see what the changes could possibly look like.

title: tvOS 27 removes a feature that some Apple TV users might miss after updating
snippet: When tvOS 27 is released later this month, Apple TV users will gain an overhauled Podcasts app. The new version includes Apple’s new video podcast streaming technology. However, eagle-eyed users may notice that the upcoming software update removes one feature that may be missed after updating: support for shows followed by a URL. more…
fullText:
When tvOS 27 is released later this month, Apple TV users will gain an overhauled Podcasts app. The new version includes Apple’s new video podcast streaming technology.

However, eagle-eyed users may notice that the upcoming software update removes one feature that may be missed after updating: support for shows followed by a URL.

Podcasts on Apple TV 4K gets a big update that removes a niche feature

As mentioned, Apple TV 4K is adding support for streaming HLS-based video podcasts in the Podcasts app in tvOS 27.

This follows the same feature coming to iOS 26.4’s Podcasts app on iPhone and iPad. The Mac also supports HLS video shows in macOS 27 Golden Gate.

But tvOS 27.0 lacks one feature as part of the new version. Shows added with a custom URL, like membership-only feeds for paid podcasts, no longer work on Apple TV 4K’s Podcasts app with tvOS 27.

This is likely a feature oversight or something that Apple plans to add back in the future.

Custom feeds are still supported for Apple’s Podcasts app on iPhone, iPad, Apple Watch, Apple Vision Pro, and Mac with the OS 27 updates.

tvOS 27 is only compatible with the second- and third-generation Apple TV 4K. The original Apple TV 4K is capped at tvOS 26 — which still supports custom URL feeds.

title: Apple invites developers to submit browser interoperability ideas for Interop 2027
snippet: Apple’s WebKit team is inviting developers to submit their ideas for Interop 2027, the next edition of the cross-browser initiative aimed at improving web interoperability. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Apple’s WebKit team is inviting developers to submit their ideas for Interop 2027, the next edition of the cross-browser initiative aimed at improving web interoperability. Here are the details.

A bit of context

Over the past few years, Apple has collaborated with Google, Microsoft, Mozilla, Bocoup, and Igalia on Interop, an annual effort to make modern web technologies work more consistently across different browsers.

The project began in 2022, building on the earlier Compat initiative, with participating browser makers and organizations identifying 15 key areas where interoperability issues were creating problems for web developers. While Compat was originally conceived as a one-off effort, it proved successful, and Interop has returned every year since.

Each year, the group selects a new set of focus areas, based in part on proposals from the web development community. Browser makers then work to improve their implementations in those areas, with progress measured through a shared set of Web Platform Tests.

Earlier this year, the WebKit team shared the results of Interop 2025, which saw the percentage of selected tests passing across all browsers jump from just 29% at the beginning of the year to 97% by the end.

They also outlined the 20 focus areas selected for Interop 2026, spanning CSS features and technologies such as the Navigation API, View Transitions, WebRTC, and WebTransport, partly based on proposals submitted by the web development community during last year’s open call.

Which brings us to this year’s open call, which officially opened on September 3 and will accept proposals through September 23.

Interop 2027 entries now open

Apple says that proposals must be based on mature web standards and be testable, since nascent technologies aren’t ready to become Interop Focus Areas, and the project relies on automated Web Platform Tests to measure progress across browsers. The company also notes that technologies that lack sufficient tests or testing infrastructure should instead be proposed as Interop Investigations.

Here’s what Apple says makes a “great” Interop 2027 proposal:

The best submissions are typically:

Specific: Identify a specific interoperability issue. One feature (or narrow group of related features) per proposal. Think font-size-adjust, not “typography”.

Impactful: Provide a clear description of the interoperability problem that needs addressing. Use cases from your own experience are especially helpful.

Valuable: Explain how web developers and/or users will benefit. Why is this more valuable than other existing options? Is there evidence this is a common need (perhaps survey results)?

Stable: Link to the stable web standard that defines the technology you want improved. (Find it on the MDN web doc for that technology. Like here.)

Tested: Look up and link to WPT test coverage. If more tests are needed, how can they be created this fall?

Read the Interop Proposers Guide to learn more.

The company also notes that developers should be mindful that not everyone reading this year’s proposals will have full knowledge of last year’s proposals, and that they must “take the time needed to fully make” their case.

That includes explaining why the proposed focus area is important, how the current state of affairs affects web developers and users, how widely the technology is used, and why addressing the issue should be a priority over other potential focus areas.

Developers can submit their own proposals by filing an issue on GitHub, or support an existing proposal by adding comments that help strengthen its case. Apple says it is better to contribute to an existing issue than to submit multiple proposals covering the same or very similar ideas.

title: Google DeepMind alumni are building tools to accelerate fusion power for the grid
snippet: Fusionality is developing control systems and simulation environments to help fusion power startups move faster.
fullText:
Sometimes founders search high and low for the right startup idea, while other times it comes to them. Federico Felici and Jonas Buchli are two of the lucky ones.

Over and over again, they heard the same thing from fusion companies: “We would ideally buy many of the components to make our our control system, but there isn’t really anybody providing them — and especially there isn’t anybody who speaks the language of fusion,” Felici told TechCrunch.

For years, the two founders have worked to develop new ways to control experimental fusion devices. “We spent quite a lot of our time solving exactly the problems that our customers need to solve,” he said. “It felt like the right time.”

To capitalize on the opportunity, Felici and Buchli founded Lausanne-based Fusionality this year and quickly raised a $3.7 million (CHF 3 million) pre-seed round from Founderful and Playfair. Felici serves as the company’s CEO, Buchli its CTO.

Fusionality is part of an emerging supply chain that has popped up to serve the burgeoning fusion power industry. Some startups, like Kyoto Fusioneering, are developing components that will help fusion startups turn their engineering breakthroughs into electricity for the grid, while others are existing manufacturers with the skills required to turn out high-precision parts.

Yet few companies specialize in the hardware and software required to control the fusion reactors themselves. “Across the industry, many companies make their own control systems from scratch,” Felici said. “But actually, 80% of each company’s control system is really exactly the same.”

Fusion power plants generate electricity by harnessing the energy released when two atoms fuse, which is more likely to occur in a superheated plasma. But plasmas are fickle, and maintaining the proper temperature, shape, and fuel level requires split-second decision-making. 

The control systems used to maintain those conditions are complex to develop and deploy, but much of the fundamental physics is consistent across reactor designs. Fusionality plans to build off that commonality to develop a suite of control systems and simulation environments which startups can then fine-tune to work with their specific design.

Felici and Buchli met while teaching AI to control an experimental tokamak — a donut-shaped device researchers use to study fusion power. Felici was working at EPFL in Switzerland, which houses one such tokamak, while Buchli was working at Google DeepMind. Later, Felici moved to Google DeepMind, where he developed simulations and machine learning interfaces for fusion devices.

Felici said AI will “play an important role in future control systems,” but that it’s not quite ready to tackle the entire challenge. “I wouldn’t be somebody who advocates for AI to take the role of controlling the entire fusion reactor,” he said. Today, AI is more likely to “complement or enhance or optimize” parts of the system, he added.

For now, Fusionality is focusing on a branch of fusion power known as magnetic confinement, an approach that uses powerful electromagnets to keep fusion fuel dense enough and hot enough to feed a power plant. Commonwealth Fusion Systems, Realta Fusion, Proxima Fusion, and Type One Energy are examples of startups developing magnetic confinement devices. Eventually, the company will develop systems for other approaches, Felici said.

Fusionality’s pre-seed funding will help the team, currently seven strong, develop a “tightly selected number of technologies,” Felici said, though he declined to specify which. He likened them to Lego blocks. “We start with a few of these blocks and then we build out more,” he said. “We have the ambition to serve the really wide range of technology that you need to operate a fusion reactor.”

Tim De Chant is a senior climate reporter at TechCrunch. He has written for a wide range of publications, including Wired magazine, the Chicago Tribune, Ars Technica, The Wire China, and NOVA Next, where he was founding editor. 

De Chant is also a lecturer in MIT’s Graduate Program in Science Writing, and he was awarded a Knight Science Journalism Fellowship at MIT in 2018, during which time he studied climate technologies and explored new business models for journalism. He received his PhD in environmental science, policy, and management from the University of California, Berkeley, and his BA degree in environmental studies, English, and biology from St. Olaf College.

snippet: The latest first-party app that Gemini Spark can control is Google Photos. The personal agent can “handle complex, multi-stage workflows” with your library. more…
fullText:
The latest first-party app that Gemini Spark can control is Google Photos. The personal agent can “handle complex, multi-stage workflows” with your library.

Available Google Photos actions that Gemini Spark can perform include:

Search & curate: Find specific photos and videos by subject, location, date, or event. Ask Gemini for the best shots and to filter duplicates.

Edit & create: Quickly enhance photo quality, apply quick fixes, and generate collages or stylized images. Any edits create a new copy that’s saved in Google Photos.

Create albums & organize: Create new shared or private albums, and save curated photos to them.

Share albums: Add or send links to shared albums in Connected Apps like Gmail, Google Docs, and Messages.

Schedule automations: Set up recurring tasks to manage your Google Photos workflows, like automatically creating monthly highlight albums or sorting photos of receipts.

Extract text from images: Find specific images and extract text from them. Then summarize or reformat the information in a Google Document, or ask Gemini to complete a task using that information.

Users can pair the Google Photos-specific features with Spark capabilities like scheduling for recurring tasks or managing their library in the background. For example: 

Every weekend, find my top photos of food, build a collage, and add it to a new album called ‘What my camera ate this week’.

Another use case is sending information found in an image to other Connected Apps (like Gmail and Workspace):

	

Check my photo of the local summer concert series and cross-reference it with my Google Calendar availability. Which night can I make it to the concert?

For a while now, I’ve relied on @GeminiApp and @antigravity agents across a wide range of use cases—spanning creativity, productivity, and analysis. But I’ve always dreamed of having a power agent to help me get the most out of my 143,206 photos and videos. And that day has come!… pic.twitter.com/WbnkYpattQ

— shimrit ben-yair (@shimritby) September 3, 2026

Other multi-action prompts include:

Find the best 15 photos from our trip to Hawaii last week. Enhance the beach shots, put them into a shared album called ‘Aloha 2026’, and draft an email with the link.

Find the best photos and videos from my recent block party and put everything into a new shared album called ‘Summer Block Party’. Draft an email to the neighborhood group with the link.

Brighten up my beach shots from my recent vacation and add them to a new album called ‘Beach Therapy’.

On the safety front, Gemini Spark creates an image copy before editing, and new albums are private by default. Spark will ask for permission before sharing albums and sending emails.

This is rolling out over the coming weeks to Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers in the US.

Omdia has published a wide-ranging report on display panels coming to new MacBooks and iPads. Based on the firm’s research into displays, it has published a roadmap of new models starting this fall and stretching into 2029.

title: We need to talk about Siri AI for Apple Watch
snippet: Siri AI on Apple Watch arrived two cycles late for watchOS 27 beta this summer. I had high hopes for how new Siri could transform Apple Watch into an AI wearable. What actually happened in July and August is that Siri has been remarkably unusable in watchOS 27 beta. Like “hold off on updating” bad. This week, I half-expected Apple to remove “Siri AI” from watchOS 27 beta 8 and revert to the previous version of Siri. Instead, I think Siri AI on Apple Watch actually got good? more…
fullText:
Siri AI on Apple Watch arrived two cycles late for watchOS 27 beta this summer. I had high hopes for how new Siri could transform Apple Watch into an AI wearable.

What actually happened in July and August is that Siri has been remarkably unusable in watchOS 27 beta. Like “hold off on updating” bad.

This week, I half-expected Apple to remove “Siri AI” from watchOS 27 beta 8 and revert to the previous version of Siri. Instead, I think Siri AI on Apple Watch actually got good?

Siri AI on Apple Watch has been a major regression this summer

The issues that plagued Siri AI on Apple Watch all summer were clear.

Siri has been slow and unresponsive. At times, Siri has been unable to do tasks like set alarms and create reminders.

Setting a timer while cooking? Go ahead and subtract at least 30 seconds from the timer to give Siri time to get it together.

Controlling HomeKit accessories with Siri on Apple Watch has also been terribly slow with watchOS 27 beta. Really, just any normal Siri task on Apple Watch: starting a workout, sending a text, you name it.

Based on two months of pre-release betas without signs of improvement, I thought Apple might need to delay Siri AI on Apple Watch. At least for existing hardware… or maybe they were just going to mess up Siri for everyone who updates? 

watchOS 27 beta 8 appears to shape things up just in time

Well, it’s been a few days since watchOS 27 beta 8 arrived, and I think all of my summer beta issues with Siri AI are just fixed now.

	

I’m always cautious to declare something resolved that could still be an issue for others. But at least in my experience, it’s a night-and-day difference with Siri AI on Apple Watch this week. I hope that’s true for everyone.

I’ve really enjoyed Siri AI for easily getting answers to the kind of knowledge questions that my curious 8-year-old son asks me. It’s especially great to do this without needing my phone. AI on Apple Watch has been a pretty big gap for the last couple of years, and Siri AI solves it — as long as it actually works.

I’m optimistic for the first time since Siri AI arrived in beta that it actually does work now. Are you testing Siri AI on Apple Watch yet? How has your experience been this summer and this week? 

(Now my one watchOS 27 complaint is that double-clicking the Digital Crown no longer jumps between recent apps… maybe watchOS 27.1 will do something with the double-click gesture. For a device so button-constrained that only the Ultra gets an Action button, it’s odd to see a double-click gesture replaced with … nothing.)

title: iPhone Ultra is coming, here’s what the final rumors say
snippet: Apple is expected to announce its first-ever foldable iPhone tomorrow, which rumors say could be called the iPhone Ultra. Here are some last-minute rumors about what to expect. more…
fullText:
Apple is expected to announce its first-ever foldable iPhone tomorrow, which rumors say could be called the iPhone Ultra. Here are some last-minute rumors about what to expect.

Starting price

In a new report today, Bloomberg said Apple was initially targeting a $1,999 starting price for the iPhone Ultra. However, due to rising component costs, Apple has most recently discussed a $2,199 starting price. iPhone Ultra configurations with more storage could stretch to $3,000, according to the report.

Delayed launch in China

In a post on Weibo today, leaker Instant Digital said the foldable iPhone will likely launch later in China than the rest of the world. This is primarily due to the device being eSIM-only, and eSIM adoption and infrastructure in China lag behind that of other countries.

The iPhone Air also launched later in China than elsewhere due to regulatory issues surrounding its eSIM-only design.

More evidence of Touch ID

In a post on social media this week, developer Pdfu shared more evidence that the iPhone Ultra will use Touch ID instead of Face ID. This, of course, has been widely reported as one of the device’s limitations, so this is just another layer of corroboration.

iPhone Ultra display crease

Apple set out to make a foldable iPhone without a visible crease, unlike other foldable phones on the market. In a report today, Bloomberg said the company has ultimately created a “crease that is far less visible than on currently shipping foldables.” To accomplish this, Apple developed an “advanced titanium-and-aluminum hinge system paired with custom cover glass.”

So even though it’s not completely creaseless, this is still something Apple “plans to highlight as a major competitive advantage.”

MagSafe

One conflicting rumor has been whether the iPhone Ultra will feature support for MagSafe. Mark Gurman had good news on this front in a recent interview. “MagSafe is there. All indications that I’ve heard are that MagSafe is in for this foldable phone,” he said.

title: Apple faces yet another lawsuit over App Tracking Transparency, with a twist [U]
snippet: While Apple has long used privacy as a selling point for both its hardware and services, I do wonder whether it now regrets introducing one privacy measure: App Tracking Transparency (ATT). For something with rather limited scope, it sometimes feels like scarcely a month goes by without a new antitrust lawsuit or regulator challenging it. A third ATT lawsuit is being brought in the UK – this one with a twist. This piece has been updated with a response by Apple at the end of the piece … more…
fullText:
While Apple has long used privacy as a selling point for both its hardware and services, I do wonder whether it now regrets introducing one privacy measure: App Tracking Transparency (ATT).

For something with rather limited scope, it sometimes feels like scarcely a month goes by without a new antitrust lawsuit or regulator challenging it. A third ATT lawsuit is being brought in the UK – this one with a twist.

This piece has been updated with a response by Apple at the end of the piece …

Personalized advertising has been one of the hot button tech topics for many years now. Instead of seeing random ads for products that may or may not interest us, we are shown ads based on our interests, as gleaned from the apps we use and the websites we visit.

In theory, this is a win for all parties. Consumers are shown ads that may genuinely interest them; advertisers get better results from their ad spend because it is targeted; while free apps and websites funded by ads get higher payments for the same reason.

Although the data used to serve personalised ads is collected in an anonymised form, the practice has led to a widespread perception of it as an invasion of privacy. Even when Apple specifically developed a technology to ensure that this data was anonymous, many consumers remained suspicious.

App Tracking Transparency

Apple’s App Tracking Transparency was designed to solve the problem by letting consumers choose whether or not their data could be used to serve personalized ads. Developers who wish to collect this data must ask consumers for permission.

Unfortunately for the iPhone maker, this has led to a whole slew of lawsuits and antitrust investigations, mostly based around the fact that Apple’s own apps don’t seek this permission. The company has on numerous occasions pointed out that its rules are in fact consistent: Apple’s own apps don’t present the ATT prompt because they don’t collect the data it references. Third-party apps that don’t collect this data are also exempted from the need to present the prompt.

The latest UK lawsuit

Apple has so far faced three complaints to the UK’s relevant antitrust regulator, the Competition Appeal Tribunal. Apple lost the first of these – though is currently appealing – and the second one is still ongoing.

Reuters reports on the third, which was filed today.

Apple is facing a £2 billion ($2.7 billion) London lawsuit brought on behalf of app developers over its app tracking rules, with the ​iPhone maker accused of abusing its power to unfairly impose ‌greater restrictions on third parties. The lawsuit, filed at London’s Competition Appeal Tribunal on Thursday, follows years of regulatory scrutiny over Apple’s App Tracking Transparency feature.

With a twist

The latest lawsuit has an interesting twist: it’s being brought by Ann Pope, who was previously a senior official with the regulator behind today’s case.

Ann Pope, a former senior official with Britain’s Competition and Markets Authority who ​is leading the lawsuit, said Apple’s policy “resulted in very significant harm ​to businesses that depend on Apple as a gatekeeper”.

“This action is important to protect ‌the ⁠rights of British businesses that depend on Apple, to ensure that the rules that Apple applies are fair, and to compensate the losses that British companies have suffered,” Pope said in a statement.

Apple recently agreed to make eight changes to its ATT rules in the EU following an investigation by the German antitrust regulator. In respect of this lawsuit, the company told us:

At Apple, we believe privacy is a fundamental human right, and we created App Tracking Transparency to give users a simple way to control whether apps have permission to track their activity across other companies’ apps and websites. Apple is bound by the exact same requirements as all developers under ATT, and this feature has been embraced by our customers and praised by privacy advocates and data protection authorities around the world, including in the UK. We disagree with these claims, and will continue to defend strong privacy protections for our users.

A number of privacy advocates have spoken up in support of ATT over the years.

title: How Tim Cook shaped Apple’s foldable iPhone, and what it may cost
snippet: On the eve of Apple’s special event, Bloomberg is out with a new report detailing the decade-long foldable iPhone development. The report highlights former Apple CEO Tim Cook’s involvement in the project. Plus, details on how much the foldable iPhone could cost. more…
fullText:
On the eve of Apple’s special event, Bloomberg is out with a new report detailing the decade-long foldable iPhone development. 

The report highlights former Apple CEO Tim Cook’s involvement in the project. Plus, details on how much the foldable iPhone could cost. 

Mark Gurman says Apple engineers started iPhone Fold development around 2016. In 2020, Cook returned home from a trip to China and was “unusually energized” about foldable phones. He reportedly pushed Apple’s hardware teams to accelerate work on the company’s first foldable. 

Typically, Cook “stayed away from the conception of new products.” Therefore, his involvement in the foldable iPhone’s development gave the project added weight:

Cook’s enthusiasm helped change the direction of the work to something that could be more mainstream. Rather than begin with a foldable iPad, Apple turned its focus to creating a foldable iPhone. “Tim was the earliest and biggest champion of this,” one of the people said. “He saw them everywhere in Asia and said Apple needed to play in this space.”

In terms of pricing for the foldable iPhone, which everyone inside Apple refers to as the iPhone Ultra, the company originally targeted an entry-level price of $1,999. Most recently, however, rising component costs have shifted that goal to $2,199. 

More recently, Apple has discussed pricing the foldable product as high as $2,199, according to one of the people, who said various options have been considered in recent weeks and that the memory shortage has led Apple to blow past its cost goals.

Some larger-storage configurations of the device could approach $3,000. Compare that with the standard iPhone, which currently starts at $799, or the iPhone 17 Pro, which begins at $1,099.

Apple is expected to debut the iPhone Ultra tomorrow. 9to5Mac will be inside Steve Jobs Theater to cover everything in depth.

title: WhatsApp for Android loophole lets private photos be accessed without unlocking
snippet: A loophole in WhatsApp for Android lets someone see private photos on your device without the device being unlocked, which obviously isn’t supposed to happen. more…
fullText:
A loophole in WhatsApp for Android lets someone see private photos on your device without the device being unlocked, which obviously isn’t supposed to happen. 

First spotted by @VBarraquito on Twitter/X and further confirmed by “Mobile Hacker” and NotebookCheck, a very straightforward flaw exists within WhatsApp for Android that allows someone to access a user’s private photos before the device is unlocked. 

This works by first having a WhatsApp call pop up and be answered – this doesn’t require the phone to be unlocked, just like a standard phone call – at which point the user can tap a button to use filters and effects on their video feed, including Meta’s AI to edit a photo – you can see where this is going. Instead of preventing access to photos, the preview is shown clearly before the phone ever asks to be unlocked with a PIN or biometrics.

This isn’t universal, though. NotebookCheck found that a Galaxy device does force the lockscreen to be unlocked before reaching this step, while Pixel and Oppo devices both allowed the full bypass. The loophole doesn’t exist on iPhone, where WhatsApp is forced to use the native iOS calling UI.

	

The plastic piece here has nothing to do with the exploit, and is presumably only for covering a contact name

The good news: this doesn’t seem to bypass the lockscreen fully, as accessing any other part of the device is still blocked. There’s also not much that can be done with the photos beyond physically seeing them – though a malicious party could use this to take photos of those images with a second device. 

WhatsApp should be able to patch this with an update, but no such update has been announced at this time. The loophole has been reported to both WhatsApp and Google. 

In the meantime, a temporary workaround is to set WhatsApp’s photo/video access to “limited” in Android’s permissions, which breaks the loophole.

title: Philips Hue adds HDMI-free Sync and new 4K Box, Nanoleaf integration, and more app upgrades
snippet: To kick off IFA 2026, Philips Hue announced a new set of sync boxes for its Play lighting. The company also teased a few new app long-awaited changes to the app, and a Nanoleaf partnership that makes your light-up triangles compatible with Philips Hue’s products. more…
fullText:
To kick off IFA 2026, Philips Hue announced a new set of sync boxes for its Play lighting. The company also teased a few new app long-awaited changes to the app, and a Nanoleaf partnership that makes your light-up triangles compatible with Philips Hue’s products.

Philips Hue’s Play Sync Box 8K is an incredible addition to any home theater or living room, but it’s expensive. At around $385, you can connect your TV’s visuals with compatible Philips Hue lights, but that isn’t a feasible option for a lot of users.

Camera-based light kits have become popular for users who want the experience without spending the money on Philips’ good-but-pricey hardware. Options from companies like Govee fill that gap for much less.

Today, though, Philips Hue announced that it’s going to offer a couple of more affordable options for users, starting with its own camera-based sync box. The Philips Hue Play Screen Sync is made up of a single fisheye camera that sits on the top of your TV. It captures colors displayed by your TV, so not only is it more affordable, but it’s input-agnostic. Unlike the 8K Sync Box, this model will work with native TV apps because it isn’t pulling from select HDMI feeds.

	

The Philips Hue Play HDMI Sync Box 4K sits in the middle of three, with a similar experience and compatibility to the higher resolution version. It only has one HDMI connection, which might make it ideal for those that just need a connection to an AVR, instead of media players and consoles.

Both new models can also opt to sync to devices through Bluetooth instead of using a Hue Bridge. That makes the setup simpler. The Hue Bridge and Hue Bridge Pro allow connections to expand to 10 lights, as opposed to a single light strip.

With that, new gradient strip lights were announced for entertainment spaces. Philips Hue says these strips will be available for TVs up to 100 inches.

The IFA announcement continues with an announcement regarding a new partnership with Nanoleaf. The company says compatible Nanoleaf shapes can be integrated into the Philips Hue ecosystem with the Wall Light Module. Those devices will work with Hue’s scenes and automations within app control.

The app itself is also getting a couple of changes. First, Philips Hue on Android and iOS will get backup and restore functionality, so users don’t lose their scenes and automations if the app is deleted or they switch phones. The app will also introduce Custom AI Behaviors, which use natural-language instructions to create more sophisticated and personalized automations by combining triggers, conditions, and lighting actions.

Both of those upgrades will roll out “beginning in fall 2026.”

The new Philips Hue Play Screen Sync will start at $119, while the Play HDMI sync box will be available for $149. Both are now available on Philips Hue’s website and retailers like Amazon.

fullText:
Google has struck a deal with MrBeast, the most popular YouTuber, to promote Gemini and Google Health, with one of the first partnerships being a challenge in “the planet’s most unforgiving landscapes.”

In a “multi-year partnership” that extends beyond YouTube, Google will work with MrBeast – aka Jimmy Donaldson – to promote Gemini and Google Health. Google says the Fitbit Air will also be integrated into an “upcoming challenge” of some kind.

An ad spot about Gemini will also feature Jimmy, showing how the AI assistant can be used to build out the channel’s infamous stunts.

Google explains:

	

As the first creator to reach 500 million YouTube subscribers, Jimmy Donaldson, better known as MrBeast, is always pushing the boundaries of what’s possible. Now, he’s tapping into Gemini to help him execute wilder concepts, showing his fans how they can use AI to help turn impossibly big ideas into reality. Along the way, he’ll also show how Google Health can support their daily fitness and wellness goals.

First up on September 5 is a new MrBeast video following Jimmy and his crew as they attempt to survive some of the most extreme and treacherous climates on Earth. Teams will race to navigate three of the planet’s most unforgiving landscapes — the jungle, the desert, and the Arctic — using Gemini to help them identify dangers, survive brutal weather changes, and stay one step ahead.

Beyond YouTube, keep an eye out for Jimmy’s upcoming spot in our newly launched Gemini campaign, where he’ll show how he uses the app as a partner to help him pull off the logistics of his signature, larger-than-life stunts. You’ll also see Jimmy integrate Fitbit Air into an upcoming challenge.

It’s far from the first time anyone has worked with MrBeast to market products. Samsung, as just one of many examples, partnered with the channel to use Galaxy phones for vlogging purposes back in 2023.

title: watchOS 27 removes three features that Apple Watch users might miss after updating
snippet: When watchOS 27 is released later this month, Apple Watch users may notice that some things work a bit differently. The upcoming software update removes three features that users may miss after updating. more…
fullText:
When watchOS 27 is released later this month, Apple Watch users may notice that some things work a bit differently. The upcoming software update removes three features that users may miss after updating.

Walkie-Talkie removed from Apple Watch

First up is Walkie-Talkie, Apple’s real-time voice communication app that only works between Apple Watches. 

Personally, Walkie-Talkie never clicked for me, especially because leaving it on meant having the yellow app icon on your watch face. Others who use it in real-world situations are already missing it, and more people will notice this month (and on new Apple Watches).

I don’t think a third-party app can replicate exactly what Apple offered with Walkie-Talkie on Apple Watch. Still, a version that works on both iPhone and Apple Watch would be better received, I think.

Multitasking shortcut is missing

Next, there’s the Digital Crown double-click multitasking gesture that now does … the same thing as single-clicking the Digital Crown. I wrote about this in my watchOS 27 public beta preview and again yesterday. 

I don’t know if double-clicking the Digital Crown will be the way forward on multitasking in watchOS. Still, a way to quickly jump between two apps or an app and the watch face has always been useful. I hope a solution returns. 

As for the double-click button shortcut, I think the Apple Watch is so button-limited that there should be something that happens with a double-click, even if it’s not multitasking. I’m thinking about this as two separate possibilities now.

Dynamic app grid always comes first

Lastly, there’s what happens when you just click the Digital Crown a single time.

Since watchOS 1 (when it was called Watch OS 1), clicking the Digital Crown from the watch face or inside an app has invoked the full app launcher. Before now, the biggest change to this system was when Apple removed the first click centering the app grid before returning to the watch face. 

watchOS 27 replaces it with the dynamic app grid: five intelligently suggested apps, the Siri app, and an icon for the full app grid. You can tap the app grid icon, or scroll the Digital Crown up to see your full grid or list of apps.

I get it. Apps aren’t super popular on the Apple Watch. The new dynamic app grid has larger tap targets with fewer icons to navigate. It also puts the Siri app in your face, which is a common theme of Apple’s OS 27 updates in general. 

If given the option, I’d probably turn off the dynamic app grid. I think it’s a fine default, but it feels cumbersome compared to just viewing the app launcher.

Anyway, change of any kind always takes a period of adjustment before it just becomes how things work. Still, I’ve been running watchOS 27 since the first day of beta 1 in June. For me, losing Walkie-Talkie isn’t something I notice, losing the multitasking shortcut feels temporary, and the dynamic app grid is a fine default, but cumbersome for speedier users.

Of course, I’d trade it all if we could get the Explorer watch face back. Removing features and changing how things work is par for the course, but removing Apple Watch faces when they’re already pretty user-removable still doesn’t make sense.

title: The Coolest Thing I Saw at IFA 2026: The Coolest, Quietest, Thinnest Laptop Concept
snippet: We could soon find ourselves in the age of actively cooled yet fanless laptops that are able to run mainstream mobile processors at full power.
fullText:
Some concepts on display at trade shows are simply bald attempts at garnering attention on a noisy and crowded show floor. And then there are others that provide actual glimpses into the future. Lenovo’s Project Aero falls into the latter category. (I’d put all of its rollable display concepts into the former: fun to see in action, but not something I’d look for in my next purchase.)

There wasn’t much to the ThinkBook laptop used for Lenovo’s Project AeroBlade concept that would get you to stop and take notice. Other than being thinner and lighter than the typical laptop, it looked like a run-of-the-mill business ultraportable. And the Project AeroBlade demo wasn’t particularly compelling on the surface. The laptop’s screen didn’t magically expand at the press of a button to draw oohs and aahs. But under the hood, there was some tech that I hope moves from concept to reality before I need to buy my next laptop.

Active cooling without fans (and their noise)

The concept of Project AeroBlade is moving air in and out of the ThinkBook without the use of any traditional cooling fans. Lenovo calls it Active Flow, a solid-state active cooling system. Instead of fans, Active Flow uses small AirJet modules from Frore Systems. We’ve seen Frore’s AirJet modules before, but this is the first time we’ve seen them in an actual laptop. 

	

			

AirJet modules use ultrasonic vibrations to pull cool air into the laptop and expel hot air out of it. These tiny modules are about the size of a mobile processing and are just 2.7 millimeters thick, and yet they are incredibly powerful. According to a Frore representative, an AirJet creates 10 times the back pressure, or suction, of a traditional laptop cooling fan. 

With four AirJet modules inside instead of a pair of cooling fans, the ThinkBook that Lenovo used for its Project AeroBlade was impossibly thin and light. It was a 14-inch laptop that was only 11mm thick, or about 0.4 inches thick, and weighed just 1.8 pounds. When I picked it up, it felt like a movie prop — an empty shell of a laptop rather than an actual operating machine.

In addition to being very compact, the laptop looked extra polished with a bottom panel that was solid and smooth. Because the AirJets are more effective at moving air in and out of the laptop, the ThinkBook could be designed without any bottom intake vents. All of the air is pulled in and pushed out of a thin vent along the laptop’s back edge.

Lenovo’s Project AeroBlade laptop looks like a standard business laptop, albeit an extremely thin and light one.Matthew Elliott/CNET

Powerful and portable

The promise of Project AeroBlade is getting higher-powered CPUs in thinner and lighter designs. With fanless laptops, you must sacrifice some performance in the form of a low-voltage or throttled processor for the thinness and lightness. 

The ThinkBook on display was running a mainstream Core Ultra 7 Lunar Lake 17-watt chip. I wonder if it’ll be able to accommodate a 25-watt Panther Lake or just a lower-wattage WildCat Lake that’s closer in thermal design power to Lunar Lake. With what about laptops we’ll soon see with Nvidia’s RTX Spark, can we look forward to a combination of a 38-watt RTX Spark and AirJet active cooling in the near future?

Read more: Lenovo’s Latest Laptop Gives Off MacBook Neo Vibes

Another AirJet benefit is acoustics. Like a fanless laptop, the ThinkBook operates in silence but with active cooling that moves air in and out. I could not hear or feel the AirJet modules’ vibrations as they worked. 

Further, without any moving parts, the laptop should last longer. Traditional cooling fans get gummed up with dirt and dust and, with their moving parts, are a common point of failure. I’d equate it to solid-state drives generally lasting longer than hard drives with spinning platters.

Lenovo’s concept fanless laptop cooling system uses two sets of four Frore AirJet modules. Josh Goldman/CNET

Lenovo wouldn’t comment on when this concept might turn into a final shipping laptop. And Frore didn’t say if it was working with other laptop manufacturers in addition to Lenovo. But given how much thinner and smaller the AirJet modules are in comparison to cooling fans, plus the fact that they can be located in different areas of the motherboard where heat dissipation is needed the most, implementing them will require a rethinking and reworking of laptop motherboard architecture. This reengineering will require some time, but I’m hoping we will see Lenovo release an AirJet-cooled ThinkBook next year. I also hope Frore’s AirJet tech will spread to other laptops beyond Lenovo’s. 

I can envision a not-so-distant future where cooling fans inside laptops become as antiquated as traditional spinning hard drives.
