title: A foldable Mac is years away, but Apple is still working on it
snippet: There have long been reports and rumours about Apple working on a foldable clamshell device that is either an iPad, a Mac, one of each, or a hybrid of the two. A recent report said that although this was once a priority for new CEO John Ternus, the project had been cancelled – but I don’t think that’s entirely accurate … more…
fullText:
There have long been reports and rumours about Apple working on a foldable clamshell device that is either an iPad, a Mac, one of each, or a hybrid of the two.

A recent report said that although this was once a priority for new CEO John Ternus, the project had been cancelled – but I don’t think that’s entirely accurate …

Personally, I think the concept of a hybrid Mac and iPad has essentially been superseded by events. There are iPhone and iPad apps that will run on today’s Macs, and for many of us, iPhone mirroring is another tool we can use to achieve the same thing. We’re also seeing increasing convergence between the operating systems, and I’m sure that will continue: we’re now long past the point where Apple was arguing that we would be converging a toaster and a fridge.

But I do think we will eventually end up with an all-screen foldable Mac once the technology exists to make a soft keyboard a viable replacement for a hard one. That isn’t going to happen anytime soon, but it will happen.

The reason I think it is still a long way off is my belief that there will be an interim step in the form of dynamic hardware keyboards. It’s literally a decade since I talked about why I think these are the future, and while this type of tech is in use today for niche applications, they still haven’t yet hit the mainstream.

The Sonder Keyboard was one early attempt, using miniature e-ink displays to remap the labels and functions of the keys.

For example, a QWERTY keyboard is almost irrelevant to someone who spends all day video editing in Final Cut Pro, which is why there’s a market for both physical keyboards and overlays.

How much smarter would it be if our MacBook keyboard or desktop Magic keyboard could adapt its labels to match the app we are using at the time?

Soft keyboards that feel like hard ones

The longer term goal, however, is entirely soft keyboards. I said back in 2016 that the very same argument Steve Jobs laid out then for virtual keys on a smartphone when introducing the iPhone could be applied equally to a Mac keyboard.

What’s wrong with their user interfaces? They all have these keyboards that are there whether you need them or not. And they all have these control buttons that are fixed in plastic and are the same for every application. Well, every application wants a slightly different user interface, a slightly optimized set of buttons, just for it.

 There are, of course, three problems with a soft keyboard:

Glass keyboards are uncomfortable to type on

We rely on key movement for feedback as well as comfort

Touch typists need to be able to feel the keys before pressing them

Apple already has patents to address each of these. First, using a flexible display rather than conventional glass can allow for deformation when a virtual key is pressed. The second problem can be solved using a combination of this movement and haptic motors. Finally, there are two ways of addressing the issue of being able to feel physical keys beneath our fingers.

Apple’s patent was for an electrostatic charge that is perceived as a change in surface texture. In other words, charges can be applied to the surface of the display to make it feel like physical keys are present even though the surface remains flat. And in 2023, researchers at Carnegie Mellon University came up with another approach.

The FIG researchers have succeeded in creating embedded electroosmotic pumps (EEOPs)—capable of moving liquids by applying electrical fields instead of using moving parts—that measure just 1.5 millimeters thick. They can be paired with an equally thin liquid reservoir beneath them, and a flexible surface structure on top, to almost instantaneously create pop-up buttons (the process takes about a second) measuring almost five millimeters in height with enough pressure and rigidity to make them feel solid when pressed.

It’s ‘when’ not ‘if’

Of course, all of this tech is still at a very early stage, but we have only to look at Mac trackpads for precedent. These still sound and feel like they are mechanical devices, but they have for years been solid-state devices that use haptics to simulate physical clicks – and they are incredibly convincing.

Soft keyboards will eventually reach that same level of sophistication. They will solve all three of the issues listed above, whether using the approaches Apple has postulated so far or new technologies that have yet to emerge.

When that happens, Steve’s arguments will apply equally to the Mac. In clamshell form, the keyboard will take whatever form makes sense for the task we are carrying out at the time. When all we need is a single giant display, be that for viewing movies or sketching using an Apple Pencil, then we will simply unfold it into a screen that is twice the size.

So I fully accept that the first generation product may have been put on the back burner for now, but that is absolutely not the same as saying it has been cancelled. This is technology whose time will come.

Those are my thoughts; what about yours? Please share in the comments.

title: Fender MIX headphones now have an iPhone app for tuning your sound
snippet: In August, Fender released the $299 MIX wireless headphones. The over-ear headphones come with a replaceable battery and the FWD Tx USB-C wireless transmitter for low-latency, lossless connectivity. Fender MIX headphones also now include an iPhone app for tuning the experience. more…
fullText:
In August, Fender released the $299 MIX wireless headphones. The over-ear headphones come with a replaceable battery and the FWD Tx USB-C wireless transmitter for low-latency, lossless connectivity. Fender MIX headphones also now include an iPhone app for tuning the experience.

The Fender Audio app for iPhone offers EQ presets and a custom five-band equalizer. This provides separate controls for low, low-mid, mid, high-mid, and high frequencies. That gives listeners a way to adjust the sound to their preferences directly from the iPhone app.

The app also includes a battery indicator and configurable Home Screen widgets for quickly accessing device actions, including EQ settings.

As for the headphones themselves, MIX features 40mm graphene drivers, hybrid active noise cancellation, and Bluetooth 5.3. Fender rates battery life at up to 52 hours with ANC enabled or 100 hours with ANC turned off.

The included USB-C transmitter supports separate modes for lossless audio at up to 24-bit/96kHz, low-latency listening, and Auracast broadcasting to multiple compatible devices.

The headphones also support wired listening over USB-C or a 3.5mm audio cable.

In my listening so far, MIX sounds great with active noise cancellation enabled. Switching to Ambient Sound, Fender’s transparency mode, sounds like a drop in audio quality to my ears, at least over Bluetooth without the adapter.

I’m looking forward to trying the app’s EQ controls to see whether I can get the sound closer to my preferences.

The USB-C transmitter tucks neatly behind an ear cushion when you don’t need it, and Bluetooth without the adapter works when convenience is more important than sounds specs.

The Fender Audio app is available on the App Store now with Fender MIX headphones support.

title: iPhone 18 Pro appears to show new colors in a retail store, but likely fake
snippet: A video shared by a leaker with some track record appears to show two of the new iPhone 18 Pro colors as part of a display at a retail store. The brief video clip shows both the dark cherry and blue colors we’re expecting, but it is almost certainly fake … more…
fullText:
A video shared by a leaker with some track record appears to show two of the new iPhone 18 Pro colors as part of a display at a retail store.

The brief video clip shows both the dark cherry and blue colors we’re expecting, but it is almost certainly fake …

The video is just 14 seconds long and shows someone holding a dark cherry iPhone 18 Pro Max, placing a dark blue iPhone 17 Pro Max next to it for comparison. We also see a light blue model on a stand.

The environment appears to be a retail store. Macworld suggests it’s possible that it’s genuine.

Given how soon they will need to appear in stores, it’s plausible that outlets will have already received demo units, although it’s obviously risky for one to allow footage to leak online before the announcements.

I’m very much more sceptical, however.

My colleague Fernando Silva recently attended the IFA trade show, and said that every single case company had dummy units that looked and felt real, so it’s trivial to obtain these. Additionally, the store environment looks sketchy to me. The display table is extremely small for a store, and the product tags appear to simply be unattached and sitting at a random angle. We also see very little in the way of a convincing store background.

Finally, while the leaker has had a track record in the past, they have more recently simply been aggregating posts from Chinese social media.

title: Apple working on new surround sound, Party Mode features for HomePod
snippet: Apple has several new HomePod features in development, based on new code references discovered in audioOS 27. The code seemingly suggests work on a new surround sound system, something called Party Mode, and more. more…
fullText:
Apple has several new HomePod features in development, based on new code references discovered in audioOS 27. The code seemingly suggests work on a new surround sound system, something called Party Mode, and more.

New HomePod features in the works 

A user on the MacRumors forums discovered the code references this week in audioOS 27 beta 8.

Most notably, the code references support for arranging four full-sized HomePod (2nd generation) speakers into a surround sound system. Currently, HomePod supports a stereo pair configuration paired as a default speaker output for Apple TV.

In the quad placement, each speaker has its own role and sound treatment. The front speakers use left- and right-specific processing, and they compensate for their potential placement close to walls and corners. Rear HomePods get an omnidirectional treatment designed to fill the space behind and around the listener.

The new tuning has a processing pipeline to manage each HomePod’s woofer and tweeters, and control bass, EQ, synchronization, and calibration data.

The code also references dynamic surround sound audio tuning. This would enable the quad HomePod system to change its processing to match what’s playing, such as movies or music.

A new “Forklift” system is also referenced in this code. Forklift appears to combine two full-sized second-generation HomePod speakers with two other speakers with an identifier that does not match any of Apple’s existing HomePod products.

Most recently, Bloomberg reported that Apple could release a new HomePod mini within the next several months. The company is also “testing a new full-sized HomePod,” but that product is not imminent. Apple released its current full-sized HomePod in February 2023.

Another new feature referenced is something called “Party Mode.” According to the code, enabling Party Mode will spread the HomePod’s sound “into a wider, more ambient mix” in order to “fill a room more evenly instead of creating a perfect listening spot in front of the speakers.”

Whether Apple actually ships these features remains to be seen. Still, it’s encouraging to see evidence that Apple is continuing to upgrade the home theater features of its HomePod product family.

title: MapQuest is back, at the top of the charts, and rushing to add Android Auto support
snippet: In a “that’s a name I’ve not heard in a long time” move, MapQuest is back to being a household name, as the original mapping app has found itself as the top of app store charts – it’s also rushing to add support for Android Auto. more…
fullText:
In a “that’s a name I’ve not heard in a long time” move, MapQuest is back to being a household name, as the original mapping app has found itself as the top of app store charts – it’s also rushing to add support for Android Auto.

MapQuest has been around for 30 years, but it only entered the modern era back in 2024 when it relaunched with a private mobile mapping app with a pitch around being “anti-Big Tech.” That app has since shut down, and a full MapQuest app arrived earlier this year.

Now, that app is at the top of app store charts.

On iOS, MapQuest is the #8 free app on the App Store (as of Aug 30), and #5 on Android’s Play Store (as of today) – at least in the US. In a press release, MapQuest says this is “the highest chart position in the brand’s 30-year history” and that usage is “roughly 50 times its normal rate.” 

	

Why the sudden surge? Even MapQuest acknowledges it’s mostly to do with a rejection of “Lake America,” with the brand refusing to update “Lake Ontario” on its platform in the wake of a recent executive order in the US which Google Maps and more recently Apple Maps have updated their maps to show. The viral nature of that stand reminded many that MapQuest even still exists, and brought about this wave of popularity.

In a bid to keep users on its app, MapQuest confirmed that it is rapidly building out support for Android Auto – it already supports CarPlay on iPhone. Android Auto added support for third-party navigation apps a few years ago, and there are quite a few options available.

MapQuest still lags behind Google Maps and others in terms of live transit and other features, but supports turn-by-turn navigation, live traffic data, and more. MapQuest is currently owned by System1, an advertising company.

title: Upgrade paths: Should Pixel 9 owners upgrade to Pixel 11? [Video]
snippet: We’ve seen a lot of people ask if making the jump from the Pixel 9 to a Pixel 11 is even worth it. The answer isn’t totally simple, but we’ll try our best to answer it here. Pixel 11 vs. Pixel 11 Pro: More similar than ever before [Video] more…
fullText:
We’ve seen a lot of people ask if making the jump from the Pixel 9 to a Pixel 11 is even worth it. The answer isn’t totally simple, but we’ll try our best to answer it here.

Pixel 11 vs. Pixel 11 Pro: More similar than ever before [Video]

Your 24-month cell plan might be coming to an end, so it’s timely to talk about this switch now, and we’ll do our best to help you decide which phone is right, which phone is wrong, and ultimately whether an upgrade is worthwhile.

An unchanged design

Let’s get the obvious out of the way at the start: the Pixel 9 Pro and Pixel 11 Pro are very, very similar. You could be forgiven for thinking they are the same. For anyone with a non-Pro phone, you’ll see more pronounced changes, but for all intents and purposes, the designs are almost identical across the entire device lineup.

Let’s get into the actual improvements. No matter what Pixel 9 phone you have, all Pixel 11 displays are better. Maybe not drastically so, but you get a jump up in maximum brightness of around 10% on the Pixel 9 to 11. The Pros get a 20% brightness jump at peak. This is something you probably would notice, but still not a major change. All the screens are well tuned, there’s no bezel reduction, just the same great experience, but brighter.

	

We know the design is the same, the core frame dimensions are identical, the same height, width, and thickness. The only visible change is in the camera bar shape and size. You can’t use your old cases on the new phone, so that is an annoyance. The Pixel 9 and 11 are within 1g, but the Pixel 11 Pro and Pro XL are almost 10 grams heavier than the 9 Pro and Pro XL. 

That could be due to the marginal battery size increases and maybe even the addition of Pixelsnap magnets, but it’s likely some internal changes that add a little extra mass, and better thermals too. Pixelsnap is great for connectivity, but a good case can mimic it pretty closely on the Pixel 9.

Similar software experience

One of the key differences between the Pixel 9 and Pixel 11 is Gemini Intelligence. It’s emblazoned all over the latest phone and adds some functionality that likely won’t come to the older devices unless Google has a change of heart.

You need to figure out if you care enough about some of the AI tools like App Automation, Rambler, the enhanced Proactive Assistant responses and replies for messaging, plus some of the other enhancements that the Pixel 10 added last year.

Some of this is merely fluff. Some are great features. Do they drastically improve your life? That remains to be seen.

Pixel 10 vs. Pixel 11: Where are the upgrades? [Video]

Even the move from Tensor G4 up to the G6 chip might not be a big enough leap for lots of people. Neither is an amazing performance beast, but they’re competent chips that handle most things you’ll throw at either phone.

Faster storage is arguably a bigger ingredient in the equation because apps will load faster, and you also get the benefit of a 256GB base model now. It was a long-overdue quality of life change that will make a bigger difference in the long term.

Frustratingly, getting less RAM on the Pixel 11 Pro or Pro XL versus the Pixel 9 Pro or Pro XL feels like a slap in the face. It’s not necessarily noticeable right now, save that you can have more apps in memory. Some of the RAM is wired for AI task control, so you’ll lose out here unless you pay more to get 16GB RAM.

The fact is, though, that the performance gap is not exactly a chasm, and Android 17 is identical here. Unless Google specifies otherwise, you’ll get all the same updates in the future too.

Quality cameras continue to impress

If you want a telephoto lens and have the Pixel 9, then yes, you might want to upgrade. The digital zoom is not as good on the base 9. It’s capped and isn’t going to get close to the action.

The other lenses are fairly similar, but know that the main sensor is slightly larger on the Pixel 11. With the default settings, it’s a toss-up.

Camera Looks are where we get some notable improvements. These are sensor-level filters that you can customize to tune your Pixel 11 camera output. No Pixel 9 will get these tools. It’s arguably the biggest change on a Pixel camera since the addition of a triple camera setup.

If you have a Pro phone, there is a better telephoto lens that lets you zoom up to 120X. Video modes get some upgrades, AI-powered Magic Capture, plus a new Creator Mode is here too.

Like basically every other head-to-head comparison, the camera improvements are more about refinement than redefining, which makes a Pixel camera so reliable.

I don’t think someone would be disappointed at what has changed, maybe underwhelmed given the two-year leap. The reality is that a Pixel camera has mostly been about consistency, which hasn’t changed.

Is now the time to upgrade from the Pixel 9 to the Pixel 11?

About upgrading: 9to5Google often gives specific product recommendations. Sometimes, we may suggest not upgrading, due to various reasons including, but not limited to: increased device cost, negligible performance gains, or environmental impact. Whether to upgrade is always your call, but our aim is to help you make as informed a decision as possible.

You don’t need us to tell you that the generational “leaps” are becoming less and less pronounced, even if you skip a few new releases.

Whether brands are holding certain functions back or other factors are at play is a topic rife among practically any industry observer right now. AI is playing a big role in the physical hardware you will buy now and for years to come.

In our eyes, there is only one key reason you should consider making the switch from a Pixel 9 to the Pixel 11, and that is if your phone is on its last legs or if you have the base 9 and want a telephoto lens. Those are the only two major reasons someone should consider the jump.

The Pixel 9 Pro and Pro XL are still fine phones. There seems to be no major or widespread issues that might cause people to be desperate to upgrade or switch away. It wasn’t the best phone on the market at launch, but, like any Pixel before, these devices tend to age better than others thanks to updates and enhancements courtesy of Google’s now-extensive support window.

	

If you’re even considering ditching a Pixel 9 Pro or Pro XL for the Pixel 11 lineup, think hard about what you’re actually getting. There isn’t anything on the software front that really warrants the substantial price increase. The new modem is good, but not a quantum leap. The camera improvements don’t provide exponential gains for photography or videography.

This is also true of most other pieces of tech right now. If your cell plan or contract is coming to an end imminently, maybe a cheap SIM plan could be a way to save cash at a time when smartphones are ballooning in price thanks to the constant march of AI development and the costs associated with the expansion.

The truth is that a two-generation upgrade cycle makes little sense today. You will simply get more bang for your buck by hanging on for another year. A battery replacement or repair would likely provide more value in most cases, given how little has truly changed over the past couple of years.

title: Syncing Hue lights to your TV now starts at $120; Nanoleaf integration too
snippet: Syncing your Philips Hue lights to your TV display used to be a rather expensive undertaking, at $385 for the company’s Sync Box 8K. A couple of new products now bring that cost down to as little as $120. Additionally, you can now integrate Nanoleaf wall panels into your Philips Hue ecosystem thanks to a new $40 Wall Light Module … more…
fullText:
Syncing your Philips Hue lights to your TV display used to be a rather expensive undertaking, at $385 for the company’s Sync Box 8K. A couple of new products now bring that cost down to as little as $120.

Additionally, you can now integrate Nanoleaf wall panels into your Philips Hue ecosystem thanks to a new $40 Wall Light Module … 

Syncing Hue lights to your TV

Synchronizing your Philips Hue lights to your TV display can create an extremely immersive experience for anything from movies to games.

The company’s Sync Box 8K uses HDMI signals to detect the colors displayed on your TV screen and then adjusts all of the Hue lighting in the same room to match in real time. At almost $400, however, it’s an expensive option, and the bundles with Gradient Light Strips can reach over $650 for the largest TVs.

The company is now offering two more affordable options:

Sync Box 4K, which also uses an HDMI signal: $150

Play Screen Sync, which uses a camera: $120

HDMI syncing is the more accurate approach, and the new 4K model reduces costs by reducing support from four HDMI feeds to just one. The maximum supported resolution is 4K at 60Hz. 

The Play Screen Sync supports whatever is being displayed, but the color matching accuracy is compromised. There are already third-party products from companies like Govee using this approach.

Nanoleaf integration

The Verge spotted that a new Wall Light Module has been jointly launched by Philips and Nanoleaf. The $40 box makes any Nanoleaf product appear to be a Philips Hue device.

While Nanoleaf products already have HomeKit support, adding Hue compatibility can be useful for third-party apps which offer more flexibility with things like animated scenes and music syncing.

title: Google’s next Pixel Fold reportedly adopting the same crease-less display as Apple
snippet: We’re still a few days out from the debut of Apple’s first iPhone foldable which, as many have expected for years, will have a crease-less display. According to a new report, Google’s Pixel 12 Pro Fold will be adopting the same technology as Apple’s foldable. more…
fullText:
We’re still a few days out from the debut of Apple’s first iPhone foldable which, as many have expected for years, will have a crease-less display. According to a new report, Google’s Pixel 12 Pro Fold will be adopting the same technology as Apple’s foldable.

The Pixel 11 Pro Fold is, as we’ve mentioned, a perfectly fine foldable. But as brands such as Oppo, Honor, and most recently Samsung have gone all-in on crease-less displays, Google’s foldable is noticeably behind. 

Review: Google’s Pixel 11 Pro Fold just barely keeps up

According to a new report, Google plans a major upgrade on the Pixel 12 Pro Fold, and they’re not the only ones. The Elec reports that Google, Oppo, and Vivo are all working with Samsung Display to adopt dual-UTG (ultra-thin glass) displays for their next-gen foldables. It’s the same tech apparently set to be used on Apple’s first iPhone foldable. 

Samsung Display and partners would be building out the display and UTG assembly to the specs of each device. This sees one UTG layer above the display, with a second layer underneath and supporting the OLED panel. Samsung achieved its crease-less display using a special titanium plate under the OLED panel, while Oppo says it filled in the area of the crease using liquid 3D printing to create an even surface along with thicker glass.

	

The report mentions that Oppo and Vivo will both have releases in the first half of 2027, while Google’s next foldable will come in the second half – probably in August, as per the usual schedule.

title: Pixel Now Playing update brings interface tweaks
snippet: The next wave of Pixel app updates is starting with Google rolling out the latest version of Now Playing with interface tweaks. more…
fullText:
The next wave of Pixel app updates is starting with Google rolling out the latest version of Now Playing with interface tweaks.

When tapping on an identified song’s three-dot button, Now Playing slides up a bottom sheet. This replaces the floating menu and is better for one-handed navigation.

You’ll see track information with side-by-side buttons for Share, Add to favorites, and Remove from history. This is followed by a button to play the song and any shortcuts specific to your connected music service.

Meanwhile, the Favorites tab now includes dates and times like the History feed. There are also icon and spacing tweaks in Now Playing Settings.

	

The redesigned Now Playing launched in March, while Google in April reintroduced the “Tap to see what’s playing” shortcut on the lockscreen.

Version 2026.08.27.x of Pixel Now Playing is widely rolling out via the Google Play Store.

This follows last month’s updates to Pixel Journal that added more tools and Screenshots (extra filter options), as well as new icons for Google Calculator, Clock, Pixel Magnifier, Recorder, and Weather.

title: Ryan Reynolds’ new Apple TV spy movie is a winner, reviews here
snippet: Apple TV kicks off its big fall lineup this week with Mayday, a new Ryan Reynolds film that’s part buddy comedy, part action spy thriller. And the first reviews say the movie’s a winner. more…
fullText:
Apple TV kicks off its big fall lineup this week with Mayday, a new Ryan Reynolds film that’s part buddy comedy, part action spy thriller. And the first reviews say the movie’s a winner.

Mayday reviews praise the film’s action, humor, and lead duo’s chemistry

Apple TV is best known for its shows, and has great ones airing now like Ted Lasso and sci-fi hits Dark Matter and Silo. But movies on Apple TV are on the rise too.

Joining the 15 free classic movies just added for subscribers, Apple has several high-profile original films premiering soon—and Mayday is first up.

Mayday premieres this Friday, September 4 on Apple TV (watch here).

The film stars Ryan Reynolds and Kenneth Branagh and hails from John Francis Daley and Jonathan Goldstein. That’s the duo behind Game Night, Dungeons & Dragons: Honor Among Thieves, and co-writers of Horrible Bosses.

Reviews for Mayday just dropped, and they’re overwhelmingly positive. Here are some excerpts:

JoBlo: “Mayday is easily the best movie not hitting the big screen this year and one of the best streaming-only releases I can think of.”

Empire: “When you hear the words ‘buddy-comedy action movie starring Ryan Reynolds’, you probably feel like you have a good idea of what to expect — some slick fights, endless witty quips, and a reasonably entertaining time. Mayday delivers on all of that, and a little bit more.”

The Hollywood Reporter: “the popcorn film proves an entertaining diversion, thanks to the mismatched-buddy comic chemistry of the two leads. It makes you hope for the hinted-at sequel”

Many reviews mention how Mayday feels like it could have—and perhaps should have—gotten a theatrical release. 

The well-executed action sequences, charming humor, and Reynolds’ lead performance all add up to the kind of movie that could have been a hit summer blockbuster in years past.

In any case, Apple TV subscribers will get to stream it for free starting this week.

title: Gemini overlay gets bubble minimization and multitasking on Android
snippet: The Gemini overlay on Android now has a multitasking option that gives you a floating bubble shortcut when you Minimize. more…
fullText:
The Gemini overlay on Android now has a multitasking option that gives you a floating bubble shortcut when you Minimize.

The Gemini overlay now shows a “Minimize” button above the container. It’s centered immediately after you enter a prompt, while the pill-shaped container appears at the right after the response.

This collapses the overlay into a bubble with the spark logo. Google explains how: “Gemini is still available while you multitask. Tap to expand. Drag to move or dismiss.”

That said, the Gemini bubble is fixed to one of six positions and cannot be placed anywhere. Additionally, a bug appears to reset the bubble to the bottom-right corner after every minimization.

	

After the response has loaded, you can tap outside the sheet to get back the bubble. Using the system back gesture will close the entire overlay, while you can also drag to dismiss.

This shortcut is a bit faster than opening the Gemini app and then the side panel to return to a conversation. Another way to use it is asking a question and then minimizing to do something else instead of having to wait for the response. 

Alternatively, you could use Android 17’s system Bubble option with the Gemini app for a richer experience.

The Minimize button and Gemini bubble are widely rolling out on Android today.

title: New profile of John Ternus offers insight into life and reputation of Apple CEO
snippet: John Ternus became Apple’s new CEO this week, and today the Financial Times published a profile that offers fresh insights into Ternus’s life and reputation among Apple employees and partners. more…
fullText:
John Ternus became Apple’s new CEO this week, and today the Financial Times published a profile that offers fresh insights into Ternus’s life and reputation among Apple employees and partners.

Latest John Ternus profile has fresh details on Apple’s new CEO

John Ternus is Apple’s new CEO, stepping into the role just days ago as Tim Cook transitioned to Executive Chair.

9to5Mac Editor-in-Chief Chance Miller has a great rundown here of what we know about Ternus, including his education, early career, public statements, and more.

But a new profile published today at the Financial Times adds fresh details and insights to the story.

Regarding Ternus’s reputation inside Apple, it says he “is known within the company for being both highly competent and unshowy.” A key Apple supply partner echoes this:

“It was very obvious from the earliest days that John was super-talented,” says Wendell Weeks, chief executive of longtime Apple glass supplier Corning, who started working with him during the development of the iPad nearly two decades ago. Weeks describes Ternus as a humble “good guy” but adds that his hobby of racing cars might give an insight into another side of his character. “There are not many non-passionate people that drive race cars…but at the same time, you have to be wicked calm and really dedicated to excellence if you’re good at it. And John is good at it.”

One former Apple executive did tell FT that Ternus is “relatively unknown outside the hardware organisation” at the company. It’s unclear how recently that executive was at Apple, however, as Ternus’s presence internally seems to have been elevated in the past year.

Tim Cook has said that Apple “really wanted this transition to be the best.” And per one anecdote from the profile, it seems like it’s been received that way internally.

the company is celebrating what appears to be a smooth handover. A party for Ternus at Apple Park on Tuesday included DJing from Apple Music’s creative director Zane Lowe. But not everyone was there. One employee said they were already so acclimatised to the change in CEO that they did not feel the need to attend.

Beyond these insights, FT does add a few key tidbits about Ternus’s otherwise very private personal life. The profile says he is married, has children, and was born and raised in California.

title: Lenovo IdeaPad Vibe is a MacBook Neo competitor starting at $699
snippet: Lenovo is taking on the MacBook Neo with a colorful new laptop – the IdeaPad Vibe. more…
fullText:
Lenovo is taking on the MacBook Neo with a colorful new laptop – the IdeaPad Vibe.

Announced at Lenovo Innovation World ahead of IFA, the Lenovo IdeaPad Vibe is squarely aimed at Apple’s most affordable and incredibly popular MacBook Neo, and it puts up a good fight on paper. The laptop can be outfitted with either a 14-inch or 15-inch OLED display and measures in at 14.9mm thick and from 2.87lbs. Thicker and bigger than Apple’s laptop, but not all that much heavier, at least in its starting weight. Lenovo says the Vibe will be available in both plastic and metal variations.

Metal
Plastic

It sure looks the part, though, with Lenovo teaming up with Pantone to offer 7 different color options for the IdeaPad Vibe including:

Dreamy Violet: a muted violet shade layered with inviting depth that inspires serenity, bringing a sense of comfort wherever it goes.

Spicy Gold: A rich golden yellow that blends warmth and energy, creating a confident, welcoming feeling.

Zen Green: A nature inspired green hue that evokes a sense of balance, harmony, and encourages a slower pace.

Chill Blue: An icy blue with a crisp modern vibe that stimulates refreshing clarity and an effortless fresh start energy.

Radiant Coral: Warm and uplifting with an optimistic orange boost that brings friendliness and positivity wherever it goes.

Moody Blue: Expressing credibility and confidence, a deep blue hue conveying refined elegance.

Lowkey Grey: A timeless grey projecting strength, stability, and understated sophistication.

The keyboard also features interchangeable keycaps so you can customize the look with some fun color combinations.

	

These are all metal versions

Pretty colors only matter so much, though, and Lenovo has stacked this laptop with a pretty enticing setup. You get a pair of USB-A ports, an HDMI port, two USB-C ports, a headphone jack, and even a microSD card reader. There’s a 5MP webcam (with physical privacy cover), an optional keyboard backlight, and an optional touchscreen on the 15-inch size.

But what’s under the hood?

You can pick between an AMD Ryzen AI 400 chip or a Qualcomm Snapdragon X chip. The AMD model supports up to 32GB of RAM which can be upgraded by the end user. Configurations also include up to 1TB of storage, also upgradable and featuring dual slots. The Snapdragon version supports up to 24GB of RAM and, while the storage is still upgradable, the RAM is not. Lenovo says to also expect an Intel version in the future.

The Lenovo IdeaPad Vibe is launching in two initial waves. AMD models will be available in October, with Snapdragon to follow in November. Both will start at $699.99, matching the price of the MacBook Neo since Apple’s RAM-induced price hike. 

Meanwhile, Lenovo is also introducing the IdeaCentre AIO I which is an all-in-one desktop computer with a 24-inch or 27-inch display, similar colors to the Vibe, and a price starting at $939. It will also be available starting in November.

title: Brydge announces color-matched keyboards for the entry-level iPad
snippet: Brydge, the Apple accessory company that came back from the dead back in 2023, has just announced a new set of colour-matched keyboards for the entry-level iPad. fullText:
Brydge, the Apple accessory company that came back from the dead back in 2023, has just announced a new set of colour-matched keyboards for the entry-level iPad.

While Apple offers the iPad itself in a choice of four colours, the Magic Keyboard for it is only available in white. That’s what prompted Brydge to launch its latest lineup … 

The 11-inch base model iPad is available in a choice of silver, blue, pink, and yellow. Brydge is now offering what it describes as a premium aluminium keyboard to match each of the four colours.

The idea is simple: you chose your favorite iPad color. Now your keyboard can match it. Most aluminum iPad keyboards are offered in traditional neutral finishes. Brydge 11.0 takes a different approach, using color-matched anodized aluminum designed to match the iPad’s own Blue, Pink, Yellow and Silver finishes […] creating a setup that looks like it belongs together, rather than an iPad with a keyboard simply added on.

The company says that it offers the build quality and features Brydge products are known for. This includes  a solid aluminium construction, a full-size backlit keyboard with 1.3mm of travel, an all-glass multi-touch trackpad supporting all iPadOS gestures, and strong magnets to hold the iPad in place. Bluetooth automatically reconnects when the case is opened.

Battery life is said to be up to three months without the backlight and a total of 40 hours’ use with the backlight on. It is recharged via USB-C.

Known as the Brydge 11.0, the keyboard is compatible with the iPad (10th generation) and iPad (A16), and costs $159. This compares to $249 for Apple’s Magic Keyboard Folio. The lineup is set to go on sale on the company’s website and official Amazon store around the middle of the month.

title: When is Apple releasing new AirPods?
snippet: Apple’s AirPods lineup is stronger than ever, but there are already rumors about what’s coming next. Here’s everything we know so far about when Apple will release new AirPods. more…
fullText:
Apple’s AirPods lineup is stronger than ever, but there are already rumors about what’s coming next. Here’s everything we know so far about when Apple will release new AirPods.

Apple’s current AirPods lineup

Here is Apple’s AirPods lineup as it stands today:

AirPods 4 (currently on sale for $99)

AirPods 4 with Active Noise Cancellation (currently on sale for $149)

AirPods Pro 3 (currently on sale for $99)

AirPods Max 2 (currently on sale for $479)

When is Apple releasing new AirPods? 

AirPods with cameras

The biggest change coming to Apple’s AirPods lineup is a new version of AirPods with built-in cameras.

This pair of AirPods will have a camera in both the left and the right earbuds. The cameras, however, aren’t designed for photo and video capture. Instead, they will be used in conjunction with Siri to provide context for the environment around you. Bloomberg has described them as “the eyes” for Siri.

For example, while looking at food ingredients, you could ask your AirPods what to make for dinner or for specific nutritional information. They might also integrate with other apps on your iPhone, such as Reminders and Maps, to provide environmental awareness features.

In terms of design, the AirPods with cameras will reportedly have longer stems than normal AirPods Pro to accommodate the cameras. There will also be a small LED light that automatically turns on when the cameras are capturing data.

The AirPods with cameras were originally slated for release in 2026. More recent reporting, however, suggests the timeline has slipped to late 2027 because of Apple Intelligence and Siri delays.

More on AirPods with cameras: 

AirPods with cameras: everything we learned this week

AirPods with cameras get their clearest leak yet

Camera-equipped AirPods reportedly won’t launch in 2026, despite demo video leak

AirPods Max

Apple just updated AirPods Max earlier this year with the H2 chip, a new high-dynamic range amplifier, improved audio quality, and more.

Last year, analyst Ming-Chi Kuo reported that Apple was working on a new AirPods Max model for 2027 that is lighter than the current design. It’s unclear whether this refresh is still on the roadmap.

AirPods 5

Apple released AirPods 4 in two different variants in November 2024, including one with Active Noise Cancellation and another without. 

Most recently, Bloomberg reported that Apple is set to announce AirPods 5 at next week’s “Surprise and shine” special event, alongside the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra. 

Like AirPods 4, the new AirPods 5 are expected to come in two versions: 

with Active Noise Cancellation

without ANC

There aren’t any additional details on what new features AirPods 5 might offer. 

Wrap up: Should you buy AirPods now? 

Apple’s overall AirPods lineup is incredibly strong, especially if you can snag a pair on sale. 

That said, if you’re in the market for AirPods 4, I recommend waiting until next week to see what AirPods 5 have to offer. 

If you’re shopping for AirPods Pro 3 or AirPods Max, I think now is a great time to buy. 

AirPods Pro 3 were released last fall with a revamped in-ear fit, improved sound quality, and a built-in heart rate monitor. I think they are truly excellent. I don’t recommend waiting for AirPods with cameras right now, since those aren’t coming until sometime next year at the earliest.

title: Apple Store is down ahead of iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone Duo foldable and more announcements
snippet: Following the usual tradition, the Apple Store is down ahead of this morning’s September Apple event, kicking off at 10 AM Pacific Time. We are expecting Apple to announce the new iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, the foldable iPhone Duo, Apple Watch Series 12, and updated AirPods (fifth-generation). more…
fullText:
Following the usual tradition, the Apple Store is down ahead of this morning’s September Apple event, kicking off at 10 AM Pacific Time. 

We are expecting Apple to announce the new iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, the foldable iPhone Duo, Apple Watch Series 12, and updated AirPods (fifth-generation).

This is the first event led by new CEO John Ternus, who has a bunch of new products to announce including the debut of the folding iPhone Duo. 

The Duo will have a ~5.5-inch outer display when closed, and a ~7.8-inch display when opened up, a bit smaller than an iPad mini in size. The Duo’s big screen, when unfolded, enables immersive media experiences, and more productivity with split-screen multitasking of two apps at once. 

Apple is expected to differentiate itself from other foldables on the market by focusing on premium build quality, including a custom-designed hinge. The crease along the center of the inner screen is expected to be minimal. 

The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max will also be launched today, including new processors, improved camera system, and a new cherry red color option. The Dynamic Island on the new Pro models is shrinking in width, resulting in even less bezel. The starting price of the 18 Pro line is anticipated to rise by about $100.

The base model iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2 will not make an appearance at this event. Apple is shifting the release schedule, so the entry-level iPhone will no longer launch in the fall. Instead, we expect it to arrive in the spring. Apple will presumably keep selling the base iPhone 17 until then.

Also today, we expect unveilings of the new Apple Watch lineup, Series 12 and Ultra 4, and new AirPods 5. The new Watches will reportedly include revamped health tracking functionality and a new AI feature that generates recaps of your daily whereabouts and conversations.

Other upcoming new Apple hardware includes a smart home display product, Apple TV and HomePod mini refreshes, and a MacBook Pro featuring an OLED touch screen. Most reports indicate these products will launch later in the year, likely as part of an October event.

9to5Mac is on the ground in Cupertino today, and we will have live coverage of all the iPhone announcements as they happen — so stay tuned for all the latest.

title: OpenAI fought dirty on career-making math problem, says NYU mathematician
snippet: There is a $1 million bounty for the first person providing a solution to the Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness problem.
fullText:
NYU mathematics professor Tristan Buckmaster announced three proofs on Tuesday with a preliminary finding on one of the major unsolved problems in theoretical mathematics. The findings, made in collaboration with Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge and using both Codex and Claude AI models, are significant in themselves — but they’re also accompanied by an unusual controversy surrounding OpenAI’s attempts to solve the same problem.

“There is another part of this story,” Buckmaster wrote in his statement announcing the proofs, “and one that, honestly, I very much wish I did not have to be concerned with.” According to the statement, a parallel effort by OpenAI built on their work before it became public, leading to a tangle of academic rivalries and conflicting claims.

Shortly after the Buckmaster’s statement, OpenAI published a full proof of the Navier–Stokes existence and smoothness problem, which Buckmaster’s findings had taken steps towards. According to OpenAI, the proof was discovered by an unreleased next-generation model, which has tackled a range of different unsolved problems over the past week. All told, the week-long effort consumed 300 billion output tokens — $22.5 million worth of compute, if charged at current Astra rates.

The Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness problem is one of the seven Millennium Prize problems — a set of major unsolved math problems, each carrying a $1 million bounty from Clay Mathematics Institute for the first person or group to provide a solution. The Navier-Stokes equations are widely used in fluid mechanics but poorly understood in theoretical terms. A solution would represent a significant advance in the collective understanding of mathematical physics.

While Buckmaster and Alpöge were finalizing their own results, they learned that “information about our progress had been passed to OpenAI.” When they contacted OpenAI, they were told that OpenAI had already achieved a full proof of the central problem. But when they asked follow-up questions about when OpenAI had begun its research into the problem and how much human input was involved, the answers became more evasive.

“It emerged that an entire team had been working on the problem,” Buckmaster said, “and that an insane amount of compute had been used…. Eventually, it was agreed that [the first prompt] had been sent in the past few days, after information about our work had reached OpenAI.”

If true, that would suggest the OpenAI team had become convinced that Buckmaster and Alpöge’s approach was the right one, and decided to use its material advantage in computing resources to reach a formal proof first.

OpenAI’s post confirms much of this timeline, specifically saying that the latest effort began on September 1, inspired by rumors that two Millennium Prize problem had been solved. Additionally, the post confirms the ongoing conversations with Buckmaster and Alpöge.

Although the problem is widely pursued among mathematicians, the specific tactic taken by Buckmaster and his collaborator is far less common. As a result, Buckmaster found it suspicious that OpenAI ended up taking the same approach at the same time.

“The route to the Clay problem through a smooth force, options c and d in Fefferman’s statement of the problem, is the route Luis and Diego opened and the one Levent and I had quietly chosen to attack,” Buckmaster wrote. “Almost nobody else I know of was working on it,” he continued. “It is not the direction one arrives at in a few days by giving a model the problem statement.”

While Alpöge is employed by Anthropic, he was not conducting this research on the company’s behalf. As a result, the duo used a mix of models, relying primarily on OpenAI’s Codex in their work. Even so, Alpöge’s affiliation with a rival lab seems to have been a sore point for OpenAI, and Buckmaster alleges that Bubeck asked him to remove Alpöge’s credit as part of a proposed compromise.

When Buckmaster pushed to make the dispute public, he says that Bubeck replied: “Why would you ruin your career?” Buckmaster says that when he pushed back, Bubeck followed up with: “If you don’t want me to be nice, then I don’t have to be nice.”

Buckmaster also raised concerns that, because he used Codex extensively in assembling the project, information from his work could have informed OpenAI’s own efforts to solve the problem. OpenAI reserves the right to train models on Codex interactions, although users are able to opt-out. If the OpenAI team used a model trained on Buckmaster’s own Codex interactions, it’s plausible that it could have regurgitated his work when faced with a similar problem. 

In its own post, OpenAI downplayed the possibility that regurgitation could have been involved. “We (the researchers and the agents) did not see any of their work through any means until they released it publicly — in particular, no specific user data was accessed in order to solve this problem,” the post reads. “While unlikely, we cannot rule out that de-identified data derived from their usage of our products helped improve our models⁠. However, our proofs differ significantly and even the precise results proved are different in the Euler case (forced vs unforced).”

Regardless, the issue is likely to reignite the ongoing debate about AI’s role in mathematical research, and OpenAI’s specific incentives. For his part, Buckmaster seems to believe the best answer is to get as much information about the research out into the public eye.

Update 2:35p.m. ET: Incorporated details from OpenAI’s release of the Navier-Stokes result.

snippet: Tomorrow is Apple’s biggest product launch event of the year, with new Apple Watch models expected to debut. And now in an unusual move, the Apple Watch SE 3 is completely unavailable in all configurations on Apple’s website. more…
fullText:
Tomorrow is Apple’s biggest product launch event of the year, with new Apple Watch models expected to debut. And now in an unusual move, the Apple Watch SE 3 is completely unavailable in all configurations on Apple’s website.

Apple’s website says ‘Currently Unavailable’ for all Apple Watch SE 3 models

Apple is expected to launch new iPhones, Apple Watch models, and likely AirPods and more at its September 9 event.

And now ahead of the event, one current Watch model—Apple Watch SE 3—has become unavailable for purchase on Apple’s website.

As spotted by MacRumors, you can configure any version of Apple Watch SE 3, then find at the end of the process that Apple’s site says the model is “Currently Unavailable.” That’s true for delivery options as well as local Apple Store pickup.

Apple doesn’t typically remove stock of a product ahead of its replacement.

But what makes this move especially odd is that there have been no rumors about an Apple Watch SE 4 coming tomorrow.

Instead, we’re expecting Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 to be the only new models.

Perhaps the current lack of availability is a system bug that will be resolved shortly. But for now, it seems to suggest that a next-generation Apple Watch SE might debut tomorrow.

title: How to watch Apple’s September 9th launch event
snippet: Apple's September 9th launch event could be one of its biggest in years. It will be Apple's first event since John Ternus took over as CEO on September 1st, stepping in for Tim Cook, and will likely feature the first models in Apple's iPhone 18 lineup. Here's how you can watch the event live, and a few possible highlights to keep an eye out for. fullText:
Apple’s September 9th launch event could be one of its biggest in years. It will be Apple’s first event since John Ternus took over as CEO on September 1st, stepping in for Tim Cook, and will likely feature the first models in Apple’s iPhone 18 lineup. That could include the long-rumored foldable “iPhone Duo,” coming just a couple months after Samsung debuted its own passport-style foldable, the Galaxy Z Fold 8.

Here’s how you can watch the event live, and a few possible highlights to keep an eye out for.

How to watch Apple’s September launch event

Apple’s “Surprise and shine” event kicks off on Wednesday, September 9th, at 1PM ET / 10AM PT at Apple Park in Cupertino, California. It will be livestreamed on Apple’s website, Apple TV, and YouTube.

The iPhone 18 might be a no-show

Apple usually announces new iPhones at its September event, but the base iPhone 18 might not make the cut this year. It’s reportedly being held until early next year, and it might end up launching alongside the iPhone 18E and an updated iPhone Air. So, if you’re looking to upgrade to one of Apple’s less expensive phones, you’ll likely need to wait a while longer.

The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max could launch with a price hike

While we might not get a new base iPhone, Apple is still expected to launch its new lineup of phones on September 9th with the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max. Both models are rumored to have larger batteries than their predecessors, and possibly a smaller Dynamic Island. They might even get a variable aperture camera upgrade that’s been rumored for years now. Leaked photos supposedly showing dummy models of the phone also hint at this year’s slate of colors, which could include black, silver, light blue, and a dark cherry purple.

Unfortunately, there’s also a good chance the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max will get a price bump over last year’s models. Apple raised prices on nearly all of its products earlier this year, and those price hikes might finally reach the iPhone during the September 9th event.

Apple might announce its first foldable phone

One of the premium phones Apple launches on September 9th could be the rumored foldable “iPhone Ultra Duo.” Images of an apparent dummy model of the folding phone leaked earlier this year, showing a passport-style design similar to Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8 and the Xiaomi 18 Fold. The Galaxy Z Fold 8 has been well received so far, with The Verge’s Dominic Preston saying it “feels like the future.” Will Apple’s first foldable be able to compete, despite being fashionably late?

The ceramic Apple Watch may finally return

Last year’s September Apple event included the Apple Watch Series 11 and Ultra 3, and there’s a good chance both watches will get an update again this year. According to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, the Series 12 could bring back the premium ceramic case option. Gurman also says the Series 12 will have new band colors and configurations, but most likely won’t have any big redesign. Aside from new cases and colors, Apple might also announce new health features for its wearables, like always-on heart rate sensing.

Apple could launch new AirPods, but probably not with cameras

It’s been a couple of years since Apple released the AirPods 4, so they’re due for an upgrade and could make an appearance at Apple’s September 9th event. However, Gurman says the camera-equipped AirPods that leaked last month won’t be released until 2027. So, if Apple announces the AirPods 5 at its upcoming event, they’ll likely be an iterative upgrade, potentially including a new chip and some new health sensors.

The prestigious television Emmy Awards began this weekend, with the winners announced for Creative Arts categories. The Primetime award ceremony is coming up on September 14th, which will include the big categories like Best Drama and Best Comedy.

So far, though, Apple will be very happy with the recognition it has gotten, with Apple TV leading the weekend with a record 20 wins. A lot of that success is attributable to the breakout comedy Widows Bay, which earned 8 wins, and is now looking likely to sweep up all the top prizes in the comedy categories.

Apple is expected to dominate in comedy, but lose out to the likes of The Pitt in drama. We’ll find out next Monday.

As it stands right now, Widows Bay has earned eight wins, Pluribus got four, Margo’s Got Money Troubles won three, Palm Royale also got three, and documentary Mr Scorsese also earned one.

title: Will Apple Bring Back ‘One More Thing’ Tomorrow? Here’s What CNET Readers Think Will Go Down
snippet: Some say the tech giant could surprise us with a Siri-powered smart home hub.
fullText:
Apple’s “Surprise and shine” event is hours away, and we’re impatiently waiting for the results of our Big Guessing Game that we’ve played for months ahead of Wednesday’s big presentation. Apple could unveil the first foldable iPhone, along with a few surprise devices and features. 

The CNET Group’s Big Guessing Game contest was held across CNET, Lifehacker, Mashable, PCMag and ZDNET. There were three rounds of predicting what Apple will unveil this year. Each correct answer earned one chance in a drawing to win the latest Apple Watch that could be announced as early as tomorrow. Before we get into your answers in the final round, here are recaps of the first and second rounds. 

We’ll be back after Apple’s announcements to share the final answers and determine the winners. 

Over 70% think Apple’s new and former CEOs will appear together

Most (71%) contest participants say we can expect Apple’s new CEO John Ternus and former CEO Tim Cook to appear together at the event. 

As of Sept. 1, Ternus is Apple’s CEO after 15 years of Cook’s leadership. Cook has become the company’s executive chairman. Ternus sent a memo to the Apple team thanking Cook and the Apple team for their work and expressing excitement for a “huge launch.” Have we ever seen two of Apple’s CEOs share the stage before? 

Cook’s predecessor, Steve Jobs, didn’t appear on stage with him at Apple’s September event in 2011. Ternus and Cook didn’t appear together at Apple’s WWDC event in June, the last before Cook stepped down, but that doesn’t mean we won’t see Ternus and Cook next week. 

Three new iPhone models are what readers expect 

Half of CNET’s respondents (50%) expect three new iPhone models next week. In round two, 80% of respondents guessed Apple’s first foldable phone would appear at the fall event. We could also see the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max models make an appearance next Wednesday. Some analysts don’t expect to see an iPhone 18 base model this year. Apple could be doing a split launch where some additional models from the iPhone 18 series lineup are announced next week and others in 2027. 

Guesses indicate the new foldable iPhone could cost close to $2,000 

CNET readers’ guesses about the price of Apple’s foldable iPhone averaged $1,847, but analysts predict the phone will cost between $2,000 and $2,500. A TrendForce report says the foldable could cost even more, starting between $2,099 and $2,299 due to the RAM shortage and increase in hardware costs. 

How much people are willing to spend on a foldable iPhone is quite different. A recent CNET survey found that US adults interested in the phone are only willing to spend an average of $781, significantly less than the expected price. 

Most think a new Apple Watch Ultra 4 will be part of the fall lineup 

Close to 3 in 4 (74%) contestants expect Apple to release the Apple Watch Ultra 4 on Wednesday, while 26% don’t think it will happen. Bloomberg reports we can expect new health and fitness features in Apple’s new watch, plus a faster chip. However, the design will likely remain the same. There’s also a chance Apple could unveil the Apple Watch Series 12 with a familiar design and biometric authentication. 

The Apple Watch Ultra 3 and Apple Watch Series 11 were both released last September, but the Ultra 2 was released 2023, with no new model in 2024. 

Readers think a foldable iPhone will be Apple’s ‘One More Thing’ moment at Surprise and Shine 

Apple is full of surprises and could unveil new devices that we didn’t see coming. But CNET readers seem fairly certain that the foldable iPhone will be next week’s “One More Thing” moment.

The foldable iPhone (18%) is at the top of the list of potential surprise reveals. It’s closely followed by a new Home hub (14%), which could double as an AI-powered smart display hub that was expected earlier this year but was delayed due to Siri issues. 

Some CNET readers also suspect Apple could reveal new AirPods (10%), and others expect smart glasses (8%) will likely be unveiled later in 2027 due to rumors of “bumps” in development next year. Some readers also predict a new Apple TV (7%), which could have an upgraded processor and Apple Intelligence.

Read and watch all of CNET’s Apple event coverage next week to learn if your guesses were correct.

fullText:
Apple has added new hardware identifiers for iPhones, iPads, Macs, and other devices, some of which could be announced as soon as tomorrow at its “Surprise and Shine” event. Here are the details.

Apple’s back end adds new products

With less than 24 hours to go until Apple’s “Surprise and Shine” event, the company appears to be preparing its back end for upcoming devices.

As spotted by Aaron Perris on X, Apple has added nearly 40 new hardware identifiers to its backend, including seven for iPhones.

A bunch of upcoming Apple device identifiers have been found on Apple’s backend. Interestingly, there are 7 iPhone models listed. We only know of 6.

iPhone19,1

iPhone19,2

iPhone19,6

iPhone19,7

Mac17,10

Mac17,11

Mac17,12

Mac17,13

Mac18,1

Mac18,2…

— Aaron (@aaronp613) September 8, 2026

Interestingly, the new iPhone hardware identifiers include one more identifier than the six models currently rumored to make up the full iPhone 18 lineup. Current rumors point to three iPhones being announced tomorrow (iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, iPhone Ultra), with the rest of the lineup expected to be announced early next year (iPhone 18, iPhone Air 2, iPhone 18e).

That said, it is possible that the extra hardware identifier could simply be a variant of one of the six other devices, rather than a new device altogether.

Back to the list, it also features nine Mac identifiers, eight for iPads, nine for Apple Watches, one for Apple TV, and three for products in Apple’s HomeAccessory category.

While most of the identifiers cannot yet be tied to specific devices, some align with products Apple is known to be developing and could announce as early as tomorrow.

That includes the Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4, a new Apple TV, the long-rumored smart home hub, M6-powered iMac and MacBook Pro models, and a new OLED iPad mini, among others.

9to5Mac will be at Apple Park tomorrow, so be sure to check out our coverage before, during, and after the “Surprise and Shine” event.

snippet: Welcome to Indie App Spotlight. This is a weekly 9to5Mac series where we showcase the latest apps in the indie app world. fullText:
Welcome to Indie App Spotlight. This is a weekly 9to5Mac series where we showcase the latest apps in the indie app world. If you’re a developer and would like your app featured, get in contact.

Calendar events can often be missed, especially since they’re usually just a notification. If you’re in do not disturb or simply aren’t looking at your phone, you might not see it. With KeyAlarm, certain key calendar events can easily be turned into alarms, allowing you to always know about what’s most important.

Key features

As the name suggests, KeyAlarm works with keywords. For example, if you set the word “Dentist”, every future calendar event with the word in the title will automatically get an alarm, saving you the hassle of having to do it individually for every instance. You can also set how far in advance the alarm will go off, to give you time to drive or commute.

KeyAlarm also supports making multiple alarms for the same event. If you want one as an hour’s heads up, then another 15 minutes before you have to be there – the app supports that, and it’ll save for future events as well.

Lastly, you can also set an alarm for an entire calendar if you’d like. For instance, if you have one calendar for family events, one for personal, and one for work – you can shift the alarms accordingly. Keyword triggering can also be done on a per-calendar basis rather than globally. This is all made possible with the new AlarmKit framework in iOS 26.

Download the app

KeyAlarm is available for free on the App Store for iPhones running iOS 26 and later. The app functions in a trial mode at first, but after 30 days you’ll need to purchase the app outright for just $0.99.
